reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Powerful Tribute to American History 🇺🇸
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visiting the Lincoln Memorial was one of the most moving experiences of my trip to Washington, D.C. The sheer scale of the monument, combined with its peaceful atmosphere, makes it a must-see for anyone interested in U.S. history or iconic architecture.The view overlooking the Reflecting Pool and the Washington Monument is breathtaking, especially during sunrise or sunset. Standing before Lincoln’s statue and reading the inscriptions from his famous speeches reminded me of the enduring values of equality and freedom.The site is very accessible and well-maintained, with plenty of space to sit, reflect, and take in the significance of it all. I highly recommend taking a moment to simply stand still and absorb the meaning behind this national treasure.Tip: Go early in the morning or later in the evening to avoid crowds and enjoy the best lighting for photos!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful monument
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln Monument in Washington, D.C is a tribute to the 16th President of the United States, Abraham Lincoln. Located on the National Mall, this memorial is emblematic of Washington with its majestic statue of Lincoln seated and its inscriptions of Lincoln’s famous speeches. It is a powerful symbol of unity and freedom, recalling Lincoln's lasting legacy in American history.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Impressive Memorial to Our Greatest President
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you have to choose one monument to visit in Washington DC, it should be the Lincoln Memorial. A fitting tribute to arguably the greatest president in the history of the country. Completed in 1922, it is a beautiful marble structure with the appearance of a Greek temple. In addition to the massive sculpture of Abe, engraved on the inside walls of the memorial are two of his most famous speeches, his Second Inaugural Speech and The Gettysburg Address. The view from the steps of the memorial of the Reflecting Pool and National Mall with the Washington Monument and Capitol Building in the distance is incredible. This has also been the sight of many protests and historic moments in the civil rights movement including where Martin Luther King delivered his "I Have a Dream" Speech in 1963. The Lincoln Memorial takes on an extra level of beauty after dark when it is illuminated. It is also less busy than during the day. It is pretty cool to walk around the backside of the memorial so that you can see the Eternal Flame at Arlington Cemetary burning in the distance across the Potomoc. The Memorial can be visited 24 hours a day although Park Rangers are available from 930am-10pm. The nearest Metro is at Foggy Bottom which is a 17-minute walk away.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Lincoln Memorial: A Must See Attraction
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most visited and most photographed attractions in Washington DC is the Lincoln Memorial. The large stone structure and the statue of Lincoln, seated in a chair, are images that most everyone will recognize. Approaching the Lincoln Memorial, you will need to be prepared to walk some steps. It seems like a lot from a distance, but once you get closer and start walking up the steps, it’s not bad at all. If you cannot walk the steps, due to being in a wheelchair or any other reason, this is not a problem because there is also a ramp. Once inside, you will be presented with the large statue of Lincoln, which takes center stage. Surrounding the statue are important quotes, including Lincoln’s famous Gettysburg address. Some will spend time reading this and other quotes, but the majority of people who visit will simply pay their respects to one of our greatest presidents, snap a few pictures, and continue on to other attractions.The Lincoln Memorial is an iconic attraction, to be certain, and it is offered free of charge. The large pillars on both the outside and inside of the building make you feel like you are entering a shrine, a holy place. Everyone is familiar with the Lincoln Memorial and most already know what it looks like from all the shared photos, but it is still a must- visit place for your next visit to Washington DC.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk to the top
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln Memorial is located at one end of the National Mall, with the US Capitol on the other. The memorial itself can be seen from a distance.There is a fairly large park area around the memorial as well as a reflection pool just in front of it, which leads to the WWII memorial.Unsurprisingly, it was busy. You can walk up the stairs or the ramp to get to the top. They were in the process of rebuilding the museum in the undercroft of the monument. Due to this, the stairs had coverings for the construction. After heading up the stairs, you see the fairly large seated Lincoln inside the building. There wasn't much else in the building other than the statue. The walls on both sides did have inscriptions. The view after heading out is quite nice, with the Washington Monument in the distance and the poll just in front.It is worth a stop since it is something that is seen quite a lot on TV and does look nicer in real life.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visit Washington, DC - it’s amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visiting Washington, DC, with my wife and our two young kids (ages 6 and 7) was an incredible experience! The historical monuments like the Lincoln Memorial, Jefferson Memorial, and Washington Monument were breathtaking. It’s something else to see these landmarks in person, especially with little ones—they were awestruck. The National Museum of Natural History was a huge hit with the kids; the exhibits are engaging and really brought the wonder of history and nature to life for them.The Air and Space Museum was partially under construction, so it didn’t have quite the “wow” factor we were hoping for. However, spending a few hours in Alexandria turned out to be a pleasant surprise; the quaint streets and charm gave us a bit of variety and made the trip even more memorable.Two downsides were parking and the cost of eating out. Parking can be a hassle in DC, so I’d recommend planning for that ahead. Dining out is on the pricier side, so families might want to budget accordingly or consider some packed meals. My biggest piece of advice? Dress comfortably and wear good running shoes—there’s a lot of walking, and you’ll want to be ready for it.Overall, this was one of our best family vacations yet! The blend of history, culture, and adventure made it unforgettable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Solemn place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lincoln Memorial is located in the Mall area. As with many monuments in the city, this one is designed in a classical style and closely resembles a Greek or Roman temple.  The 19-foot-tall statue of Lincoln looks out from a solemn chamber in a building surrounded by 36 columns, each representing a state in the union at the time of Lincoln's death. Admission is free and the Memorial is always open, except for Christmas. In addition to being a symbol of the city, it hosts many events and is famous for being the venue from where Martin Luther King Jr delivered the “I have a dream” speech in 1963. In this period the memorial is subject to important work for the construction of a museum dedicated to Lincoln. Despite the work the charm of the monument does not fail, it should be a bit more respectful and less noisy, remembering that it is still a memorial. If there was more silence the place, with its beautiful view of the Mall, would be phenomenal.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must See in Washington DC
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited twice, once on our own in the day time and later, on a night time tour.  Both times it was crowded (though less so at night).  In the day time it was very crowded, and it is worth patiently navigating your way through the crowds to view this impressive monument up close and take in the speech inscribed in stone, and other information about the 16th President.  (A little useful tip: underneath, there are public toilets - not always easy to find in US cities).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Park Police are strict!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have lived in Washington for 20 years, and used to work in very close proximity to this Monument for almost 15 of those. So I have been to this Monument many times, and sat on its steps to eat lunch and have gone during work hours just as a little break to sit back and awe at. Of course I have taken several guests there at night, and it's really beautiful and a magical place to be. I do recall hanging out at the monument with an ex-boyfriend and we had coffee with us. We attempted to sneak around to the back side and consume our hot beverages during the cold weather as it was raining. It really would have been a truly romantic evening and a much more memorable experience had the Park police not kicked us out for having food and drink, or rather drink on the premises. This was just coffee mind you and nothing illegal. We weren't doing anything else other than just wanting to have a private defensive place to sit and enjoy a record and the Magical atmosphere. So if you do go, I recommend you don't bring any hot beverages, or any food or beverage that would be consumed on the monument premises. It's a wonderful place to go and be pensive, but I think they want people to just come up see Mr Lincoln, take a few pictures and then go.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful memorial!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln Memorial has always been my favorite memorial in D.C. and it's likely because Lincoln is one of my favorite presidents. It's a stunning tribute to him and it's a very thought-provoking place to be, even when it's absolutely crowded. The architecture of the building itself is gorgeous and that is only enhanced by the statue of Lincoln himself. My favorite way of seeing this is it lit up at night and the memory of that is one that I will keep with me forever. It's a beautiful memorial and one you should make sure to see once in your life.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Where History Rocks and Abe Rules!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's a classic. 'Nuff said.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The first time I came to Washington DC, I missed this entirely. Not that I didn't know what it was (I've seen the Tim Burton Planet of the Apes, after all), but that I just never got the chance to see it. I've now been to DC four times, and I made sure to see it one the latter two. And as a history enthusiast, let me tell you: this is worth seeing in D.C. Is it a tourist trap? Oh, absolutely. It's crowded with schools and other visitors day and night, and it's genuinely time-consuming to get there and back via walking (unless you're looking for a lengthy walk, which you might be). But it's worth it for sure. Say what you want about glorifying the founding fathers of any country, but you FEEL the glory standing in front of this statue. You have to wonder if Honest Abe would like this monument, and I imagine he wouldn't really be a big fan of it personally. But his accomplishments certainly warrant his commemoration, and this is a more-than-worthy way to do so. It's a must-see attraction if you're in the city, that's for sure.Now I just need to get to the MLK monument, dammit...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Respect!

If you are visiting Washington D.C. and your hotel is close to the mall, the mall is quite easy to reach by walking and to reach all sites is easy even if you are handicapped. The Lincoln Memorial is likely the largest and most iconic memorial at the Memorial Mall. This memorial highlights the life of Abraham Lincoln,  it shows his ideas, statements, speeches and his relevant decisions on emancipation and liberty.  Entrance is free. It also offers wonderful views of the National Mall, the pool, and Arlington.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A wonderful and fitting memorial honoring Abraham Lincoln
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C. is located at the western end of the National Mall at the opposite end of a long grass strip from the Capitol building. Visiting the Lincoln Memorial can be challenging if you are driving since finding parking can be a challenge due to its central location. I recommended utilizing public transportation or parking at nearby garages and lots, such as the Union Station Parking Garage or the Ronald Reagan Building and International Trade Center Parking Garage. You could also take a guided tour or utilize ride-sharing services. I rented a car and toured several sites that eveningThe main entrance to the monument is by broad steps on the eastern entrance. As you approach the memorial, the grandeur of the structure becomes increasingly apparent. The iconic 19-foot seated statue of President Lincoln commands the attention of all who visit. The larger-than-life figure exudes a sense of strength and wisdom, while the inscription of his immortal Gettysburg Address and Second Inaugural Address reminds us of his profound impact on the nation.The memorial's interior is a large chamber, adorned with murals depicting significant moments from Lincoln's life. The marble walls and wide spaces create an atmosphere of reverence and reflection. From the steps of the memorial, visitors are treated to panoramic views of the Reflecting Pool, the Washington Monument, and the U.S. Capitol, forming a breathtaking vista that encapsulates the spirit of the nation. It is not only a tribute to a remarkable leader but also serves as a gathering place for historic events and peaceful demonstrations. Its significance in American history and its architectural grandeur make it a must-visit destination for locals and tourists alike. The lighting on the steps at night is very limited so step carefully. If you were only going to see one monument in DC, I would choose this one.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded but must-see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln Memorial is a monument in Washington DC dedicated to Abraham Lincoln, the 16th President of the United States. It is located on the National Mall and is one of the most popular tourist destinations in the city.When there are a lot of people at the Lincoln Memorial, it can be a bit crowded and hectic. Visitors may have to navigate through crowds and lines to get inside the monument, especially during peak tourist season.Despite the crowds, the Lincoln Memorial is still a must-see destination. The monument is an impressive structure with 36 white marble columns and a large statue of Abraham Lincoln inside. The walls are inscribed with some of Lincoln's most famous speeches, including the Gettysburg Address and his Second Inaugural Address.Visitors may need to be patient and wait their turn to get a good view of the monument or to take a photo. However, the crowds also add to the energy and excitement of the experience.One tip for dealing with the crowds is to visit the monument early in the morning or later in the evening, when there are fewer people around. This can also provide a more peaceful and serene experience, and allow visitors to take in the beauty and grandeur of the monument without the distractions of large crowds.Overall, the Lincoln Memorial is a must-see destination for anyone visiting Washington DC, and despite the crowds, it's worth the effort to visit and pay tribute to one of the most important figures in American history.

reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stop by when walking the mall.  Pick a sunny day.  Take the metro or take your chances finding parking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sightseeing tour
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fascinating monument, of a nations leader. Exhibit below is worth the visit.  Access for wheelchairs and toilets for everyone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lincoln Memorial is well worth the trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely beautiful. Made chills run down my spine. What a tribute to our nations history. And we stayed until dark. The ambiance was amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great experience better to see in person recommend to wear comfortable sneakers lots of steps to get to the monument 🥰
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very impressive monument didn’t imagine how big the monument is in person and is also a beautiful view from there back 🥰🤗

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Old Soldiers Never Die...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Time to revisit this photo we look in December 2013 of what looks like the ghost of a soldier walking behind our 3 granddaughters (gray figure). We had just been to the WW2 Memorial, and the figure looks like it is wearing a helmet and flack jacket. Photos taken by other members of our family at the same time show no one in gray behind or around them. Just an old soldier passing by, we guessed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see memorial with view along the mall
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the must see sights in Washington, it can be quite a serene place to enjoy the view of the mall and take in some history if you can shut out the crowds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love this Memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This Memorial is great.  No trip is complete without a trip to see Abraham Lincoln.  It is amazing how much detail is in the monument.  I highly recommend seeing this one in the daylight as well as at night.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best at Night
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing monument so much better to be seen at night as quite crowded during the day. Plus it is far more focussed at night with the lights, very powerful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You have to go here if visiting Washington DC, there is a lot of history here + it appeared in Forest Gump. A great place for photos & worth walking around the back & underneath where there is a small exhibition.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: MUST SEE
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one you have to see and I imagine every time you see it, it is as amazing as the first time.   It was very crowded the day we went but wouldn't miss it as it is awesome.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great, but needs work!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As this was at state capital, I would’ve wish to have seen it more clean and kept up with. I went with my mother who is handicapped and she couldn’t go up to see Abraham Lincoln because the stairs were too much plus there was too much people. On top of that, the people there were a tad bit disrespectful to the monument which was also disheartening. Overall, it was a nice visit, but there needs to be better keep up of the place. The inside where the history is explained smelled like feces and the elevators were out of service which posed an inconvenience to everyone who couldn’t go up the stairs included my mother.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Everything you thought it would be
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The memorial area was very clean, and it was an enjoyable experience. We went on the Moonlit Trolley Tour and seeing it lit up at night was very nice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awe-Inspiring!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Having seen the Lincoln Memorial so often, it was a not to be missed destination. Going in the beginning of October was a great choice because the crowds were small and the weather perfect for all the walking. We were able to get great pictures, spend time reading Lincoln's words, and reflecting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Site worth visiting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is very impressive in person. I guess due to the weather it was not very packed and we where able to take pictures and walk around the grounds. Our team where able to see fort hand and stand on the same spot where magnificent Figueroa have given speeches that changed history. It hits you different when you can actually be there and see the size of this place and compare it to what you’ve seen. It changed or teens perspective on the whole thing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Well worth it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The statue is beautiful and very moving to see it in person. The quote on the wall behind Lincoln perfectly encompasses who this man was, and the magnitude of what he did, which is hold the country together. You can’t visit DC and not see the Lincoln statue.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have wanted to see the Lincoln Memorial for years. It didn't disappoint. Very inspiring! We just sat for a while taking in the views and our surroundings. Highly recommend!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The building itself is just breathtaking, the statue and scripts on the wall are also very beautiful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very impressive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very clean memorial, not too many people around which made it easy to read the scripts on the walls.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved it so much it was amazing I loved it it touched my heart and soul and was the best thing I have seen on this trip

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A "must see" experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful, historic monument. Easy walking to the Korean monument. Cafe and loos in easy walking distance, pretty lake. Very moving.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This Memorial is excellent. There’s a small museum like inside. There’s also bathrooms available. You do have to climb a lot of stairs but it’s worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must-See on the Washington Mall
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited in Fall season, and if you have the chance I'd suggest you do the same, as this can  be a very busy area of the Washington Mall.  The Lincoln Memorial is at the far west end of the Mall, and if you're like us, you'll find yourself walking from one end to the other making as many stops as your time allows.  If you visit the Washington DC Metro website, you'll be able to see that the train and bus lines make stop/s along the Mall.  I remember the 1st time we were in DC about 10 years ago, We bought what was I think a multi-day pass, used the heck out of it, and our car didn't leave our hotel the whole time we were there!But, back the the Lincoln Memorial.  It wasn't as crowded, as I stated the BUSY tourist season was over.  Such a beautiful building.   If you're able, take the time to walk around like we did, and take in the different views of the city at every turn.  Also, don't forget a good pair of shoes and have you phone charged, as you'll be taking SO many photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So much history in one place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This trip was my chance to show my 8 year old daughter the memorials and this was her favorite.  We were able to ride up on an electric scooter, find some parking areas on the edge, and walk up.  It was the same monument and yet different.  Took her to stand on the spot of Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I have a dream" speech.  You look out towards the Washington monument across the reflection pool and you can think about all of the other people that have been there and stood where you are.  There is just nothing like it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great view and very educational
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a very well taken care of monument and very educational. Please take your children here and also your family so they can have a great time walking the national mall

reviewsWithKeywords.title: America's own Parthenon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just amazing, in awe!  The statue the structure, the atmosphere, the grandeur unparalleled A bucket item for sure for American and foreigner

reviewsWithKeywords.title: In on memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Large memorial which was crowded with tourists and very hot outside. Worth seeing along with all the other memorials

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Missed out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to DC recently to see a bit of history. Well a bit is all we saw. Travel through DC is a challenge to say the least. No one there seems to be tolerant of any type of traffic, so if you slow down to be sure you're turning on the right street because you're from out of town, or you slow up just to look at a site, you are honked at, yelled at, and given the finger. Lovely welcome for tourists - thanks!So after two days of fighting traffic and rude people, we cut our vacation two days short and decided if we were going to get to see any of the monuments or sites, we'd have to leave the hotel to get on the road before daybreak so no one would get mad because we were holding up traffic.We left our hotel at 4:00 A. Knowing nothing would be open to tour, we still wanted to get pictures of the more popular sites, such as the Lincoln Memorial. Imagine our disappointment when we found out you can get pictures of every side of the monument from the road/car EXCEPT the side old Abe is actually sitting on. Unfortunately, I am not able to walk a great distance, so even in the regular business hours, I wouldn't have been able to walk up any steps, but I had hoped to at least view the memorial from the car and get pictures. Nope, not able to do so. Not that we could see, anyway, but it's hard to see everything in the dark.Not to mention, with all the security around DC in general (which obviously is a good thing) you don't really push to try to get in somewhere that looks inaccessible as you don't know for sure if it looks that way by accident or on purpose, because you won't want to end up in custody for fear of them thinking your there to do some dastardly deed.The sheer size of the building is amazing and breathtaking, but I sure do wish we had gotten to see Lincoln.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very impressive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A long hot day in August walking around the National mall, Gwen you finally climb all the steps the monument is ver impressive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must.. to see in person
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I'm not sure how anyone would say this is an average attraction... really.. if there are 5 things you must see when in DC.. this is one of them.  Its grand during the day but its spectacular at night.   Lots of parking at this end of the mall, but the walk from Washington monument to the Lincoln Memorial is something else.. its long but well worth it.. the size and scale of this memorial leaves you speechless.  The history, the significance, and the stature of this memorial is a must see in person and stand at the feet of Lincoln Statue

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Washington DC memorials
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a check off the bucket list. It was my favorite part of my whole trip, I didn't want too leave knowing all the history and bravery accomplished here. You would have thought I would have taken more pictures, but my emotions got the best of me. It was extremely crowded, everyone seemed to be drawn by the history. It was truly larger than life and a day I won’t ever forget.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent in the evening
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must do when coming to Washington, and I recommend going in the evening, because the shadows add character to an already stately monument. Be sure to walk into the rotunda and read the inscriptions and literally stand at the feet of a giant. The perspective is amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lincoln Memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The  feeling of pride when you visit the Lincoln memorial is amazing. The different kinds of marble, limestone and why there was so many different type speaks to the inclusion of many states during it building process.To stand on the top step and look toward the Washington Monument,  was breathtaking!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely awe inspiring and beautiful  A must see.  Stairs may be difficult for some.  Getting to the top is worth it.  Would recommend to all.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great view, and great monument. Interesting speech on the side. Best appreciated with some background reading about it to understand its symbology and importance.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy but Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful monument, crowds were very manageable, lots of vendors around selling $1 water or Gatorade (just dudes with coolers, probably illegal but as a consumer I was happy), the only issue I had was the bathroom area located nearby (just off of the reflection pool) was in a terrible state. Extremely dirty, both urinals were out of order and one of the two stalls also. Stood in line for nearly 15 minutes because of this.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Memorial, great visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Always wanted to see the Lincoln Memorial as it's an iconic site. A must see when visiting Washington DC. There were a lot of tourists and at times it was hard to obtain a clear photo but it's worth the walk from our hotel. Visited in July and the weather was very warm but the memorial is surrounded by trees and shade. It was a lovely experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lincoln Memorial-Free Entry, Stunning at Night.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln Memorial is one of the top destinations in DC. Entry is free, and we decided to visit at night when the air was cooler and there was a bit of a breeze.The statue of Abraham Lincoln is much larger than it seems in photos, and the side walls are engraved with two of Lincoln’s speeches.  It is a place filled with honor and thoughtful reflection. Also, make a point to stop near the top steps to find the marked location where Martin Luther King Jr. delivered the historic “I Have A Dream Speech”.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awe-inspiring, America at its best.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln Memorial makes one think what America is at its best.  A time to reflect on the past, present, and future.  The grounds surrounding the Memorial are beautiful.  A definite site to see when visiting Washington, DC.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Get your pic and go
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's really crowded, even at dusk. The gift shop is really small - basically a closet. Go ad get your iconic picture, but don't spend a lot of time here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always a fun stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was crowded with college groups when we went, but still a good place to visit. Lots of stairs. Not too far from the parking at the Tidal Basin.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Going there is mandatory if you’re in DC. I had never been there at night, and even when it was crowded it was wonderful to see the lights. I prefer visiting early in the morning, when there is just a few people.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic and perfectly placed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked here on our first full day in the city.  It's sited at one end of the mall, which is the focal point fo the city, and opposite the Capitol Building situated at the far end.  The memorial is breathtaking with Lincoln sitting prominent and powerful in the centre, looking out towards the Washington memorial in the centre.  You have to climb some steps to get up to the monument and, with Lincoln facing you, there is an engraving in stone on the wall on the right with his second presidential address and his Gettysburg address on the wall on the right.  There are lots of people selling water and Ice Creams outside.  There are restrooms at the base of the monument on the left as you look upwards.  However, due to the significant amount of use they get, they appear not very well maintained.  As a monument it is fitting to a man of great standing and an absolute must for anyone visiting the Mall.   We also visited at night when we did an evening bus tour.  The photo's accompanying this show the different vista's.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous! Especially at night
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went during the day and returned at night to see this stunning monument. Even our children and grandchildren were awed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Impressive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: take a walk from Washington monument to Lincoln memorial. You can take beautiful pictures while walking along the mirror pool. The memorial is impressive in size. Inside Lincoln is watching over you towards Washington monument.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see in DCA real historical monument and place.The vies from the memorial is just great and you only miss Forest Gump being there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the absolute greatest monument buildings in the entire (history of the) world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: PROS* Stand in awe at one of the world's most iconic famous and meaningful structures* Fantastic structure- an architectural marvel* Tremendous statue in thoughtful pensive pose- gigantic* A monument to our guiding principles and future as a nation* It feels like a temple or a shrine* A historical place to remember the events here through the ages* Unparalleled and unequaled views in both directions- the National Mall and towards Arlington National Cemetery* Learn about Lincoln from his speeches engraved on the walls and from the information downstairs* Free and unfettered access 24 hours a day* Celebrate its 100th anniversary in 2022* Bond with our nation's past and commit for a better future* Best later at night or early at dawn in the morningCONS* It can be always crowded* Tour groups (especially school groups) can be rowdy and disrespectful* Tour group guides speeches disturb the solitude that is an essential part of this shrine* Motorized and pedal bicycles roam freely at the base- dangerous* Truly inadequate lighting at night- dark! (see my many photos)- a danger for the visually- challenged"I VISITED THIS PLACE"...... as the first and most important stop on my nightime monuments tour for my family (we visited the adjacent Vietnam. Korea and MLK but did not get any further that night).  As stated and as seen in my many photos, the place after 2030/2100 was very crowded with noisy groups and it is quick dark and could be downright dangerous to thos who are disabled- and that was at night!!  Maybe everyone is learning of the secret to come at night, as I've posted on the TripAdvisor D.C. forum for years.So we returned at 0700 the next day and there were still plenty of people there, but it was much more managable, yet certainly not quiet nor solemn.  We walked around the entire perimeter of the building, at the level of the statue.This place deserves more than five starsTIPI've always said and written to go at night; now I add go at dawn PLEASE see my many photos- from night and from day and then from various lookouts, perches and observation points and backgrounds.  If you like this review and/or the many photos that will be attached, please click "helpful."

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Impressive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The size of this memorial is something pictures can not do justice to.  It is massive.  It is something you see your whole life in pictures but to finally stand here and see it is such an amazing moment.  Then to also find the exact spot that Martin Luther King Jr. stood when he gave his speech just adds to the moment.  Turning around and see the reflection pond and the Washington Monument just adds to the moment.Overall, this is a place you see your entire life but when you finally are standing in front of it, you are still taken aback by it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Such a great place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I really liked beeing there, it is such a beautiful place from american history. When you come to Lincoln Memorial, there is a view on beutiful lake, I recommend it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family Travel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We learned where the exact spot was that Dr. King stood during his historic speech in August 1963. This was something that we had thought about for years.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Who doesn’t love Lincoln?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pros:CleanHistoricalSeemed safe, lots of cameras everywhere Could get very close to itYou were even able to ride scooters/bikes/etc around it! Cons:Like every monument in DC, this place was extremely crowded. Like, really super crowded. Good experience. I definitely recommend.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don’t Miss It!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing place that makes you proud to be an American. The history behind the memorial is very interesting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Outstanding, educational and those stunning views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: 21st May and the 4th stop on our tour of the National Mall. I didnt grasp the size of this memorial until we were actually there, the entire monument is huge, from the steps leading up (turn around for that magical view of the Washington Monument across the Reflecting pool), the statue of Lincoln himself to the enormous tablets of his famous speeches adorning the interior walls. In all honesty this was something that genuinely took my breath away. Aside from the great statue, there is also a museum underneath that provides some educational benefits, especially to those of us from another country!!Outside on the steps, with that view across the reflecting pond, there is also a marker depicting where Dr Martin Luther King stood to make his speech, it is there but you may find that many people are unaware of it and are simply standing on top of it to take in the view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Memorable
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was on our daughters “bucket list” and we all loved it! It is amazing to see and it is right there with other attractions, best of all it is free!  DC does have public restrooms.  We got an unlimited metro pass so we could ride all the trains and busses and not have to worry about a car.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lincoln
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The memorial was absolutely incredible.  It was mesmerizing and seeing it with your own eyes is amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: early morning visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My daughter and I walked from hotel early morning (0630), sunrise amazing and no one else at memorial.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just an amazing memorial to see.  Beautiful structure and area.  First time taking our kids and it definitely made an impression.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bucket list item!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was on a business trip to Washington DC recently and couldn't not visit the Lincoln Memorial and other nearby attractions like the Washington Monument. I've seen these in so many movies and TV shows over the years.It was no disappointment either, with so many sites close together within walking distance and the Lincoln Memorial itself was an oasis of cool on an incredibly hot day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have always seen photos but to see the memorial in person is amazing.  There are about 40 steps up, but they are separated with a platform so you can take breaks in between if needed.  You can capture an amazing view from the top of this memorial of the Washington Monument and reflection pool.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Even crowded, this is SO worth it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful; be sure to read all the quotes on the inside.  A must see for historical reference from our 16th president.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It doesn’t disappoint, you’ve seen it on tv loads but actually going is a very spiritual thing - even to a non American. I went in the morning and it wasn’t too busy, also near the Korea, Vietnam and WW2 war memorials

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Touristic sites!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was very nice walking in the park leading to the Lincoln memorial, the surroundings green areas and the water give you a feeling of peace and quiet even when there are many people around. The weather was a bit hot and humid though so you need to have water on you at all times.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When we arrived at the National Mall, our first stop was the Lincoln Memorial. When you see it in person it is absolutely amazing. Being there and remembering President Lincoln and all he meant for this country is such an incredible feeling. You would think it's just a stone monument and statue, what can you possibly feel, but until you're there then you will know.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A great place to start!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Parking around the mall and monument will be primarily using ParkMobileApp. Go ahead and set this up before getting there. Gift shop inside the monument. Go early in the morning to get the best pics with less crowd. Seeing monument at night is just as beautiful but harder for pics.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't forget the small museum underneath
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is an iconic memorial that is breathtaking inside and out.  To fully appreciate the memorial, you must visit during the day and at night.  The views at night are just stunning and will take your breath away, whether you are looking up at the Memorial from the bottom of the steps, or away from the Memorial toward the reflecting pool toward the WW2 Memorial, Washington Monument and Capitol or inside.  You do not have to walk up the iconic steps as there is a ramp but if you can walk up the steps you should.  Once inside, as you see the giant statue of Linoln, the words of the Gettysburg Address and other famous words of Lincoln are etched on the walls.Do not neglect the small museum at the base of the memorial.  Many people skip over that or don't know about it.  It doesn't take long to go through.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Truly stunning! It’s hard to pick a best time to go. Maybe early morning to beat the crowds. But it’s gorgeous at night when it’s lit up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see in DC
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An amazing place to be in. So much history around and beautiful located monument, overlooking the Reflection Pond and great view of everything leading to Capitol Hill. Breathtaking!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Silent Night
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of ways to experience this memorial, my favorite is getting a coffee from Starbucks (about 3 blocks) and sitting on the steps overlooking the reflecting pond at 9pm.  Very quiet and private way to take it all in.  Park police are usually nearby and it's well lit.  Your mileage may vary.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see whether first time trip or 50th.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see for anyone visiting DC. The Lincoln Memorial is an absolute icon in the city. What more can be said about a place that has been the focal point of so much recent history? The downsides are that the steps are very slippery, so be careful going up or down the steps. The crowds are enormous and constant, so be prepared to wait for that perfect photo. Additionally, the crowds are anything but respectful and quiet while inside the memorial itself, which can be overwhelming for those who have adverse reactions to loud places or auditory input from many sources/angles. Despite the above critiques, this is a bucket list level spot for anyone’s first time to DC (and also for the 50th time).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lincoln Memorial a must visit memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Each time we visit DC we love to walk through the Lincoln Memorial. It is so special. Beautiful views and of course honors our country.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see in DC
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see in DC. Beautiful grounds and inspirational history. A tribute to a great man that has to be experienced in person.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was fun to take our 4 daughters here to see the grandeur of this structure. It's really astounding. We were able to take electric scooters from this location to another after our visit, which was super convenient.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Atmosphereric
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited this memorial following our walk/bike around other sights at the national mall. Walking up the steps and seeing the national mall behind us and seated Lincoln in front was stunning and thought-evoking. The neoclassical style of the building itself was quite pleasing and matched other sights in DC. Both interior walls on the sides included excerpts from Lincoln's inauguration speech and the building included a mini gift shop and restroom, albeit dirty as expected. Whilst the memorial was packed with tourists and kids, we were still able to enjoy the full atmosphere of the monument and to look back at the US's deep history.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Please visit here in the early morning.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was raining on April 5th around 4 pm. There were a lot of people. I went downstairs. There was a small museum for Abe. The next day, in the early morning, I visited the memorial again, it was empty and quiet. Probably, the early morning is the best time to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So beautiful but THE busiest memorial... I recommend maybe going at the end of the day or first thing in the morning

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A moving experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I find the memorial very moving.  It was a lovely day and the pandemic was dying down, so the memorial was pretty packed. Even with the crowds, you can enjoy this very large monument with its stunning views of the Reflecting Pool and the Washington Monument.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must go to
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not real crowded in the early hours. A must see at night. Donn't miss the view of the Capitol Building from standing in front of Abe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Always a beautiful place to reflect on the amazing works of Abraham Lincoln.  They were cleaning the reflecting pools when we were there so that changed the view a bit for us, but still beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth It!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My 7 year old was super excited to see A.L. memorial. For us it was amazing. Tons of people and I would suggest to go early.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see, despite the crowds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Must see, despite all the crowds. The scale of the monument is huge, as was Lincoln's impact on our nation. They offer a Junior Ranger program through the bookstore for the kids, and it ended up being a suitable place to take a rest.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Quick Visit to the Lincoln Memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went on a random day of the week, around 11am, when it had been drizzling out so it was pretty quiet in the area.Nothing new to report on the Lincoln Memorial that hasn't already been shared but it was impressive up close!  You know it's huge but seeing it in person is astonishing!  We didn't have enough time to really read everything but we stayed for a few moments to admire the monument and then left.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Weekend trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Way too busy for me. Awesome site though. Nice. Really cool. It’s pretty big. I should have looked to see how big it actually is.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely a lot bigger than I thought. Loved walking all around it and seeing the inscriptions.  Very busy area so I would suggest coming earlier in the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must See DC
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is such a fantastic memorial. The size alone of Lincoln sitting in his chair overwhelms me every time I visit. You can't visit DC without visiting Lincoln. We went at night, before 9p in March over a busy weekend and even at that time, the monument was filled with people and tour groups.It will always be crowded, so be prepared for that, but don't let it deter you as this is a must see while visiting DC. Make sure to stop and pay respects on the steps to Martin Luther King Jr. and look out over the reflecting pool, imagining the hundreds of thousands of people who flocked to see him give his most famous speech.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Brilliant
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I’ve seen the Lincoln memorial on films and on tv but I’ve never quite appreciated how massive it is! The statue of Lincoln is amazing. He sits in a neoclassical temple. It is elegant, clean and breathtaking. You can see where Martin Luther King delivered his ‘I have a dream’ speech on the stairs.The view in front of the memorial is amazing - the reflecting pool is great and then on wards to the Washington monument.There are toilets to the left of the memorial as you look at it and a small exhibition on the memorial which was good.If you’ve not seen this before and are in DC you need to go see it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of my favorite stops in DC!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see.  Only wish we had more time to spend.  We went at night and the view is breathtaking.  Do not miss seeing our great president, even if only for a minute.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the stairs

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What An Iconic Memorial! Worth A Look!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The giant memorial to 'Honest Abe' is such an iconic structure that I had to visit when in Washington DC. It sits near The White House and on The Mall with The Washington Monument. Not to forget The Vietnam Veterans Memorial. An excellent picture of the The House of Representatives (The Capitol Dome) may be taken whilst at the memorial. All within walking distance. Some things I picked up on. It is in Greek Revivalist architecture (based upon The Parthenon in Greece), it has 36 columns because of the 36 states that were part of the union at the time of Abe's death, and has 58 steps, which represent his two years in office and being 56-years-old at the time of his assassination. Spend a morning or all day taking in these amazing structures. It really is great sight-seeing!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Lincoln Memorial…
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My first visit to The Lincoln Memorial many years ago was during the day; however, a nighttime visit is a must.  It is amazing to see the memorial illuminated at night.  The Lincoln Memorial is an exquisite creation that pays homage to the president that saved the union.  In addition, there have been so many other defining moments that have taken place at The Lincoln Memorial such as Dr. Martin Luther’s King’s I Have a Dream speech given on August 28, 1963.  Visiting this monument definitely provides an opportunity to think about historical moments in time and how one man’s presidency helped to shape the United States of America.  The Lincoln Memorial is one of the most impressive monuments that you can visit at the National Mall.  I encourage everyone to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It is not a safe place to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was my first time visiting DC, but my wife had been several time in the past. What I noticed right off was the level of tension in the air. It's very hard to describe. It was cool to check these places off the "must do" list. Now having said that, I did not feel safe at all. Open air drug market, homeless and lack of law enforcement is very disturbing. If you dare to wander off the footprint of The Mall area, it's straight up chaos. I won't go back and if I had to recommend a trip to a family member, this would the last place on this coast. What was odd though, was the level of security for all the government buildings. There was a ton of security, uniformed and plain clothes. Once you cross the street it's a free for all and just plain dangerous. Part of my visit required that I travel one night and on the way back, the streets were overrun with gang activity, homeless everywhere and no law enforcement to be seen.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Meaningful Visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I visited the Lincoln Memorial in June 2021.  You can find metered parking nearby on Constitution Avenue.  It costs $6.90 and the parking meter accepts credit cards.  There is a time limit.  I walked to the Lincoln Memorial.  I have been here many times.  I had just visited several Civil War battlefields so this visit had a lot of meaning.  The Lincoln Memorial was very crowded this time.  I read the words of Lincoln's Gettysburg Address and Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address.  The Lincoln Memorial book and gift shop was open.  The staff of the book and gift shop were very helpful and gave me National Park Service brochures.  Finally, I found the marker for Martin Luther King's "I Have A Dream" speech.  I had been searching for this in past visits and finally found it.  All in all a very meaningful visit to the Lincoln Memorial.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: As Lincoln said For the People!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln Memorial is a US national memorial built to honor the 16th President of the United States, Abraham Lincoln. It is located on the western end of the National Mall in Washington, D.C., across from the Washington Monument. Taking the form of a neoclassical temple, the memorial's architect was Henry Bacon. The designer of the memorial interior's large central statue – Abraham Lincoln, 1920 – was Daniel Chester French; the Lincoln statue was carved by the Piccirilli Brothers.[3] The painter of the interior murals was Jules Guerin. Dedicated in May 1922, it is one of several memorials built to honor an American president. It has always been a major tourist attraction and since the 1930s has been a symbolic center focused on race relations. The history of this glorious building is more than incredible as the man who is depicted within it. Lincoln was a man of many attitudes feelings and ideals who was fought almost all the time. During the Civil War he had to actually fire a very famous General who was a friend of his. His name was McClellan, for some reason this general couldn't figure out when to fight!Lincoln it is said actually visited him and fired him replacing him with a big mouth cigar chewing General Named Grant! Well Grant got it done alright. We all know what happened to Grant now don't we?The building is in the form of a Greek Doric temple and contains a large seated sculpture of Abraham Lincoln and inscriptions of two well-known speeches by Lincoln, The Gettysburg Address and his second inaugural address. The memorial has been the site of many famous speeches, including Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech, delivered on August 28, 1963, during the rally at the end of the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom.Like other monuments on the National Mall – including the nearby Vietnam Veterans Memorial, Korean War Veterans Memorial, and National World War II Memorial – the memorial is administered by the National Park Service under its National Mall and Memorial Parks group. It has been listed on the National Register of Historic Places since October 15, 1966, and was ranked seventh on the American Institute of Architects 2007 list of America's Favorite Architecture. The memorial is open to the public 24 hours a day, and more than seven million people visit it annuallyThe day i was there I am an Opera singer. I stood with my wife and stared at the beautiful statue of Lincoln a man i so thought was a hero! While I was standing there I was tapped on my shoulder, I turned around and a person recognized me. So I looked at her and did. Boy the place went crazy she cried, my wife cried, everyone was clapping, but It was only good because of whom i was singing it for. The Man on that great statue, the greatest people in the world Americans. But for the Greatest Country in the world The United States Of America!God Be with you all my friends as always ...pace e amore   Carl

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What would he be thinking?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln memorial was one of the highlights of my visit to the capital. It is a grand tribute to the greatest president in US history. The Gettysburg address is chiseled in on one side of the building and the second inaugural address on the other. As the nation today stands more divided than ever since the civil war you can’t help wondering what Lincoln is thinking as he is gazing out on the capital from his chair.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Moving, Must-See Memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My son and  visited the Lincoln Memorial on our recent trip to DC.  The Memorial is one of the signature monuments in DC.  It is a beautiful monument and grand in scale.  It sits at the opposite end of the National Mall from the US Capitol Building.  The memorial contains a very large statue of Abraham Lincoln seated in the center of the monument.  The statue is posed to reflect the two sides of Lincoln, the firm Lincoln who vowed to stop the Southern States from secession and the conciliatory and the kind Lincoln who wanted to welcome the Southern Stars back as brothers at the end of the Civil War. It is a very moving monument.  Also the views from the top of the steps are terrific.  You can see the reflecting pool and the Washington Monument and the Capitol Building and more.  This is a must see in Washington.
