reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is just something about DC that makes you really stop and remember where America started and I credit this to all of the amazing memorials. We took a night time tour of the memorials which was beautiful to see everything all lit up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Favorite
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice park, building and memorial you get to see here. Luckily it rained the day prior but not the day of our visit. You easily spend 2-3 hours walking around. The statue of Lincoln is huge. Bigger than I saw it previously in movies. He was an impressive personality.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful building. Just like in the movies. The Gettysberg Address on one side and his second Inaugural address on the other with Lincoln in the middle. Also a plaque outside on the floor where Martin Luther King delivered his famous 'I have a Dream' spech

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Quick cold visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sorry it was cold the day I visited.  Always a great place to see.  You can climb stairs and take pic looking over  water to the WW2 memorial.  It was cold & windy this day!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing - Not to be Missed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I’ve always wanted to see it.  Sometimes when you finally see a monument you’ve always wanted to see there is a let down.  Not this one. It was even better than I imagined.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: From the moment you approach the memorial from the WW2 memorial it’s clear to see how grand this is. Beautiful building with great time and care keeping it as such. Humbling place to visit and the silence was respectful while within the main hall. Worth a visit by walking the mall if you are fit and able. Great view toward the Washington monument from the top of the stairs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Birthday Weekend
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a magnificent place to visit. I’ve always wanted to visit the Lincoln Memorial and I finally did this for my birthday. I can’t even tell you how it felt standing and watching people just chat and take pictures. What and amazing feeling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Classy memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I visited the Lincoln Memorial with a group of students and loved it. It is so very massive and the scale can't be contemplated without a visit in person. My niece (7) asked me to take a picture of the back, so I endulged her. It was peaceful, since literally no one else was back there. So glad I went (front and back)!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful at night
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was my first time going at night.  The lighting was beautiful and bright of Lincoln.  Also, seeing the rest of DC from the top of the stairs was so beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must do when Washington
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was definitely worth doing!Even though it was busy it was amazing.Views looking out from the memorial it is beautiful.Worth going too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Always a pleasure to see. The park is clean and well maintained.  On the list of must see, while in D.C.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning at night
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must see site, but to enhance your enjoyment, consider seeing it a night with a tour guide. The location of the Lincoln Memorial and its size make it truly impressive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Family time
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This Monument is huge, beautiful and breathtaking. We made it at night time and it’s great. Beautiful pictures of the Capital Building.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So serene and vast and stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You see it in films, in pictures, on TV and it never compares to how it feels to be there in person. The stillness of the water against all the surrounding memorials and waving American flags is just so beautiful and peaceful. Washington is one of the nicest cities I have ever been to. Absolutely loved the Lincoln Memorial, it's stunning and so well looked after. Well done America, it's a masterpiece.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great part of history. Enjoyed reading his speeches. Wish people would have given the memorial more respect. Kids running around yelling. Was just beyond rude.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lincoln Memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Always seeing other people's photo's of this great memorial, it was on my bucket list for many years and finally it became a reality.  This beautiful monument is situated at the end of the Mall, but it being a lovely sunny winters day, there were crowds of people.  Very beautiful on the inside and great history! If you are unable to climb those stairs, you can take the old elevator up to the chamber and see Lincoln himself! It is also nice to just sit on the ledge on the back of the monument and plane watch! Definetly recommend!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must See
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a cold, windy night but I am so glad I went. What a beautiful tribute to a man who did what only he could do. Thank you President Lincoln.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful landscape around the site. The memorial is stunning and quite big. It’s a must see memorial in the city.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful monument, great to plane watch at, great history on inside
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful monument and not very crowded. Very beautiful on the inside and great history! Take the old elevator up to the chamber and see Lincoln himself! Sit on the ledge on the back of the monument and plane watch! Definetly recommend!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: amazing in person
reviewsWithKeywords.text: the weather was rainy the day that we visited, but it was still amazing to walk along side the reflection pool and walk up to the memorial.  It was ALOT bigger in person than I think I had imagined it was.  But we didnt have to fight people to get photos' and it was really neat to see in person.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So cool to see in person
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you love history you have to check it out. Without seeing it in person you cannot understand the experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is a must visit for all history buffs out there. Lush green environment. Good place for family with kids. GIves a clear view of the Washington Monument and US Capitol.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing. A must see.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The grandeur of this Memorial looking over the reflection pool has to be visited to be experienced in all it's glory. Seeing the it in real life is amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best by night!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The honor given to this great man is show in the beauty of his memorial. The view from the Washington monument across the pond to the memorial is beautiful. But it is best see up close in person. Walk from one end to one end & walk up the stairs to his statue. Read the famous quotes & remember what he fought to abolish & the movements he made to start advocating for women. Tip: Parking is difficult, walk in from the Metro or take the DC Circulator!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was there with my family during the holidays of course there was hundreds of visitors in spite of that you get this sense of awww and peace that I cant describe. I don't know if it was the building or the history behind this memorial but I would definitely revisit. My family enjoyed this trip so much!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Knowing the history that comes with this monument, it is overwhelming. The view at the top looking outside towards the Capital is just as breath taking as the view looking inside at true seated Lincoln statue.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Weekend Getaway
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Awe inspiring and fabulous!!Took a moonlight tour of all of DC but this was our favorite! Every about was amazing. Would definitely visit again’

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see in DC
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You must visit the Lincoln Memorial while in DC.  It's a stunning sight and a feeling of reverence is felt immediately.  This is truly an American treasure!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: impressive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: very impressive to visit, we were lucky we went in December when it was quiet as we got to stay longer.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see in DC
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you live in DC or are just visiting you must go to the Lincoln Monument, I go at least once a month just to center myself.  The statue of Lincoln takes my breath away and I am always pleased to see that once inside the monument even the most boisterous visitors seem to be taken over by the serenity of President Lincoln and the meaning of the words etched on the walls.  Of course the view from anywhere around the monument is amazing, but my favorite is sitting on the steps looking towards the Capitol.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful monument
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a lovely place to visit. On the trolley routine so easy access. Everyone enjoyed the space around it also. Lovely outlook.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must do!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful memorial which if you are lucky enough to see on a sunny clear day is a MUST see!  Historical and mesmerising.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The legend preceded this place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can’t stop at the mall without visiting old Abe. This place has a very real aura of civic pride about it and it’s always popular with visitors. It’s on the far side of the mall from the capitol so a lot of walking but it is well worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Was there and I had a great time. The view was nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went around the memorial. Interact with people who were also there on visit. I would recommend that the best day to visit should be weekdays. It tend s to be too crowded during weekends

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Washington's Parthenon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln memorial very much has the appearance of a colonnaded temple and also has the vast feeling of a cathedral. Our visit during the day was very busy and it was difficult to appreciate the architecture and the fact that it is a memorial. We returned during the evening where we able to enjoy this enduring symbol in spectacular lighting, definitely a better time to view if you can.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Check out the exhibit downstairs!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln Memorial is by far one of the most amazing things about DC. It will always be a "must see" of any trip. What we didn't know about was the cool little exhibit downstairs by the restrooms. It's very small, but really neat! It's mainly photos of the competition to see what the design would be and different events that have taken place there over the years.  It will only take about 10 mins to walk through, but was a nice little bonus!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The busiest memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is always a busy memorial. The amount of different languages heard on the steps is a tribute to the impact this man had, not only in the United States, but a reputation that goes worldwide. Truly impactful . 4th visit in my lifetime.    Little known fact, the Memorial and Washington Monument are perfectly aligned to block the Capital building.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We tried to take our kids here last time we visited the area, but due to illness, we weren't able to see this monument. We are so glad we tried again and was able to see it this time. We loved this monument. The size is unreal and the work that went into making it is just amazing. We are glad that we stumbled upon the history of it near the bathrooms, otherwise we wouldn't have known about all the rich history. The size of the building overall is incredible. Although there were many people coming and going, we felt we were still able to stand and enjoy it and get good pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Imposing — as you would expect
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I would like to visit it again but very early in the morning before the tourist hordes arrive as it was way too busy when i was there and it detracted from the experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Favorite place to spend New Year's Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I lived in DC for 7 years, and for 3 of those years I watched the sun rise on New Year's Day. It's a remarkably beautiful place, especially at sunrise in winter and sunset in summer. If you come here in. the morning after a fresh snowfall, it's magical. I try to avoid the place when there are lots of tourists.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is not to be missed. I didn’t know all the history behind this but we visited the small museum underneath and I learned a lot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of DC’s gem
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a good place for family or friends. You can walk around or just sit on the stairs and  and enjoy the reflecting pool view with the monument in the background. It’s a good experience on any given time of the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing structure
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful site a long walk from the capital building, but along the way there are many very important structures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Interesting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The monument is so big. Always has a lot of people taking pictures. The view is amazing to the the reflection pool and Washington Memorial.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great  Memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a stunning experience.Impressive, highly meaningful statute awakens the respect inside. We visited it by day and night, take time to walk around. Highly recommended.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth the walk to visit this Memorial. The statue of Lincoln is impressive and humbling. Highly recommend going.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must go place when visiting Washington DC. The memorial in gorgeous and Lincoln statue impressive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing site
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Impressive site. Never went to visit last time and did today So glad we did. Cool place. Amazing history and the view ..is spectacular

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Running Destination
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visible from the entire mall, this Memorial marks the Southern End. If one were to run around the Capitol and this Memorial, the loop would be about 5 miles. The running paths are safe, clean and well maintained. Except for the paths closest to the Reflecting Pool next to the Lincoln Memorial, which are covered in goose poop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful to see but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to Washington in December over Christmas break thinking it would be cooler and there would be less crowds.  It was cooler, in the 60's when we were there but that was warm for that time of year and people were out in droves because of it.  The reflecting pool makes for GREAT pictures.  I just wish there had been less people in the picture.  Everywhere in the Mall area is a hike so be prepared!  I suggest if you are older and don't excersize much, start walking a couple miles regularly before you go.  Even if you are taking a shuttle or other transportation, it is a hike from parking lots to monuments.  In the area of the Lincoln Memorial is the WW1, WW2 and Korean War Memorials and the Washington Monument is at the other end of the reflecting pool.  All very walkable even for us 50+ but you had better prepare.  Definatly worth the effort!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and awe inspiring
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited the Lincoln Memorial on a gorgeous afternoon in December. We walked from the portrait gallery to the memorial – it’s a lot farther than you would think. We passed the world war two memorial and also visited the Vietnam veterans wall. The Lincoln Memorial It’s just all inspiring once you get up the steps and into the memorial. The book shop on the upper level was nice. And it’s a must see monument if you’re in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Inspiring
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This for me was the highlight of our trip.  The monument of Lincoln is awe inspiring and his words are moving.The view from the steps back onto the Mall are breathtaking.You can also stand where Dr. King gave his speech.  Loved my visit here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Still inspiring
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln Memorial never gets old with three or four visits a year. If you are able to avoid busy evenings it is better. Don’t expect for it to be as serene as it was in Mr. Smith goes to Washington, but it it’s still moving, especially if you take the time to read the walls.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful piece of history
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to visit Lincoln Memorial in April. It was pretty warm that particular day but it was worth it. The walk of the National Mall was tiring but very educational for our kids that are 7 and 9 years old. A must visit place  for al ages.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful at night
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love this place. Beautiful at night when you can look over at the Washington Monument. Only problem is it is a long walk to get there

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful at night!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We decided to go to the Lincoln Memorial at night with our teens. It did not disappoint! Breathtaking views! We felt safe visiting at night too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful landmark to visit! We went at night which had a dramatic feel. The view of the Washington monument was beautiful. Lincoln's memorial monument is amazing! Definitely get a guide to fill you in on the historical architectural facts. Very interesting!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always Impressive.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We brought visiting teenagers downtown for the first time and they enjoyed the Lincoln Memorial. It was mid to late afternoon on a Saturday, so pretty crowded. I love the immensity of the place, and the reminder to not forget an important piece of our past.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lincoln Memorial at Night
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to see the sites at night while they were lit up. Fantastic. So quiet and smaller crowds. Always wanted to see this monument, really enjoyed it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This memorial is really impressive . I love this place . It’s beautiful and peaceful . When you stand next to the Abraham Lincoln statue you feel powerful. Better to go early to avoid the crowd .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: See at Night and Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A MUST see at night and during the day. Total different experiences. Both equally amazing. Grab some hot coco and sit on the steps in the evening. Its really nice and beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the most popular site so expect lots of people. We went towards the end of our day at around 7pm thinking it would be quiet! It wasn’t. If you want it to yourself, go at 6:00 a.m. to be fair everyone is very considerate and you can all get the picture you want for the album! Well worth it as it really is iconic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful and well maintained. There is an elevator and restrooms to the left of the front of the building. We saw it at night and during the day.  The only downside was we were visiting Thanksgiving week and it was crowded.  Impossible to get a great picture with other people in your shot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: More than lived up to expectations. A wonderful tribute to an inspirational figure of American history. Cracking view back across the mall to the Monument and Capital Building beyond

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Historic and beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must place while visiting the capital . Try and go in the day and after sunset to see the reflection pool.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Memorial of a popular President
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good to visit a beautiful memorial of a popular American president..popular place for all tourists visiting Washington..Long water body and surrounded by a well maintained park

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Some history here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great to come here and stand where Martin Luther King did and imagine 250,000 people crammed in. Also where Forrest Gump was! Nice to walk the length of the pool up to the ww2 memorial. Be prepared as it’s constantly busy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous at Night!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went at night to avoid crowds, but also because it’s one of the things available after the museums close at 5pm.  The walk along the reflecting pool at night from the Washington monuments and the WWII memorial is beautiful.  I felt completely safe as there were other people around.The best part is how beautifully illuminated the monument is.  It’s stunning in person and you have time to read and reflect without having to dodge people taking selfies.  And, as most of DC, it’s free!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Girgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice place with gorgeous view inside and outside the memorial, a must see if you are in DC. Plan on going on a sunny day for nice pics and to walk around the mall.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great to visit again
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is actually one of the last stops I had on a whirlwind 2-days in DC. Hadn't visited the Lincoln Memorial in a two years. Heavy rain that day and chilly temps on this last visit Dec 21. Still, it takes your breath away to see Lincoln in grand scale every time. Small hidden gift store inside has a remarkably well stocked collection of books and souvenirs.  I agree with others- even in the cold, its nice to stand at the top and take in DC

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Majestic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtaking! A grand structure for lovers of history and architecture. It’s close to other notable memorials and tourist location as well, so it’s a great midpoint pit stop too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Patriotic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I love this place! Amazing sculpture and relaxing just to hang out at the reflecting pool. Just hard to take pictures without the photo bombers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great visit to Lincoln Memorial. Try to visit in early hours otherwise from 11am on it is crowded. Forewarning you will be dodging people on scooters everywhere so be on the look out. There is also a tiny gift shop to the right once up the stairs and at the monument. Overall great experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nightime viewing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What an amazing monument and to visit at night added more to the experience. A must for all ages to take a moment and stand before this magnificent tribute to a man who was ahead of his time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Four score and seven years ago
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although the last time I was in DC was back in 1997. Lincoln still looks the same clean as a whistle. Although,  the elevator is as old as time, bathroom extremely dirty oh and the water fountains have never been replaced. One would like to believe that they would have replaced them. Maybe instead of the White House getting a fence replacement project. Disappointed that the grounds in several areas seem to be totally run down.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Run With Abraham Lincoln
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Three way to go. 1. Park at Arlington Cemetery if you run early morning. Run straight across Memorial bridge to Lincoln and continue down our National Mall to Washington Monument (between is exactly 1 mile). Take in sights of Smithsonian, Museum of Natural History and you've gone another mile. 2. Park at phone parking above Reagan National on Potomac River. You can watch airplanes turn overhead to land. Sometimes you will see Marine 1 plus one. Run between GW Parkway and Potomac turn when you see Lincoln and head down the National Mall.3. Start at Oronoco Park in Alexandria and head toward power plant going along the Patomac. So nice that part. Then run around Reagan Airport and head across Memorial Bridge. You will see the golden guardian statues guarding access to Lincoln. Look for protector of the Union, US Grant.I always go around watching Lincoln who is watching us all.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awe inspiring and majestic. A historical delight!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the must see historical buildings in DC. Just to be standing in front of the memorial, understanding the founding history of the US, and walking around this majestic memorial is enough to give you goosebumps!!The building is one of the must sees along the National Mall with the others being the White House, the Monument, The House of Senate, The Jefferson Memorial, The Smithsonian Museums, and (further back) the Martin Luther King Memorial. Highly recommend a visit if you’re in DC. Enjoy your trip!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always amazing to see and such a site at night!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: While we've seen it a number of times over the years. It's still amazing, with incredible architecture, and what a great huge carving of Lincoln.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always amazing to see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A visit with Lincoln is always amazing, the architecture is impressive and the sight of Lincoln is breath taking. I have visited several times over the years and he is one of my top 3 to visit. I do love the view of the Mall from the top of the steps looking back at the Capital.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Spot to Honour History
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the Circulator here, and then walked back towards the Washington Monument.  On a sunny Saturday it was too crowded, and lacked the reverence one might wish.  Lots of selfie takers.  Take time to take your shots, up, down and all around.  Consider the impact of Lincoln and how America might have been without him.  Read the words of Lincoln on the interior walls -- today some should take more time to respect these thoughts.  A powerful place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lincoln Memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was pretty cool taking pictures at the Memorial. Lots of walking, but lots of great photo opportunities. Don't miss the exhibits on both sides of the memorial.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Jaw dropping and stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As the pictures show it can get very busy but once you climb those steps, you have a beautiful view of the memorial mall. It is such an interesting piece of history (one of many in dc) that you must visit. Just take your time with the walking as things appear closer than they are

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Historic sight
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This memorial is a must see for anyone visiting Washington. It is beautiful,  historic,  and offers a beautiful view of the reflecting pools, Washington monument and Capitol building.  I would recommend two visits, one in the day, and the other at night. It offers two different perspectives.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: History and grandeur
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After a lovely Walk along the National Mall the Lincoln Memorial looms on the horizon. It's one of those moments when you realise how big something is in real life! There are a lot of steps to climb to reach the top but there is also a (very old but safe) lift if the steps are too much. Totally worth it! A great way to learn more about the history of the US.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This place is attractive and awesome
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lincoln Monument is built to pay tribute to America's president Abraham Lincoln. It is a very beautiful place, clean and secure, and huge. You will definitely get beautiful photos here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Monument
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This monument is amazing. It is an impressive sculpture of Abraham Lincoln. I think everyone should visit this monument.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Night tour is way to go
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went at night while it was lit. It was a stop on a tour bus, well worth the $$, especially in the cold temperatures. The National Mall at night is beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Lincoln Memorial Enough Said
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If your visiting the capitol either for you first time or returning then this will not disappoint, its grandeur and splendor is amazing, worth seeing in the day light as well as night time as all lit up is a amazing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely, especially at night
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing view of the Washington monument and next to Vietnam memorial.  Very moving.  My 11 year old went in and read the Gettysburg address on the wall.  Very relevant.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lincoln Memorial at Night
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went on a nighttime monument tour while on vacation in DC.  I would strongly recommend visiting all the memorials at night first and return in day if you want more time.  The Lincoln at night was amazing and the right way to round out the tour; you also visit the WW II memorial which is also great at night.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Like all of central Washington this is beautiful to behold . We were very impressed. As a capital city it is so splendid.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: On our way to FL
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the evening to drive in and through DC.  Plan parking in advance and walk the grounds in and around the White House and mall area. It’s HUGE!  Quite impressed.   Officers everywhere are very helpful with directions and or parking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning masterpiece
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved the writings inside to remind us of how far we've come and how far we have yet to go. Stunning views of the reflecting pool and monument.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Memorial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was there late in the afternoon, so I was able to see the memorial in the day and night.  I really feel it’s more impressive at night.  It really glows and draws you in.  Sitting on the steps and looking towards the Washington monument is a very peaceful feeling.  Thankful for all the freedoms we have and thinking about all those who have been right there on those same stairs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Grandiose monument
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Seeing the statue up close is impressive and amazing! I never thought I will be so happy to see this historical monument so close!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful monument
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful stop anyway, but to see it at night is amazing!  We did the trolley hop on during the day & their tour for the night time one too. They were also great to work with to get to the monuments.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visit at dusk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I went at dusk, it was absolutely awesome! We look forward to bringing our children. The grounds are beautiful and the walk from the Washington memorial is great

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The building and the statue is big and very impressive. But too crowded if you want to wait for a good photo spot

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Awe inspiring and breathtaking. Must visit in DC. Do visit both in day and night and take time to read the speeches engraved on either side of the walls.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: He's Massive!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is hands down my favorite monument!!! I've always loved Lincoln so that may have something to do with it!! Super cool to stand on the exact spot where MLK Jrs "I Have a Dream" speech!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Impressive site, small Lincoln
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The whole parade up to the actual memorial is very impressive. The column building around the statue is also impressive. But once you are inside, it is amazing how small Abraham Lincoln is as a monument. He's suspended high because he is on a pedestal which is on a plinth, but the actual man himself is smaller than expected. This aside, the whole experience of walking up and going inside is amazing. Highly Recommend.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Brilliant
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Memorial to the Capitol Building is a beautiful part of Washington from end to end. The walk between the two is long but absolutely worth it.The monument itself is as grand as you’d expect with some nice quotations (from the Gettysburg address and his inauguration?) on the walls.It’s pretty busy all the time but the views are stunning and great for photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must See
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Lincoln Memorial is one of the most iconic and moving places I have ever visited. Lincoln's message still resonates today.  All of the amazing speeches and rallies that have been made there is very emotional.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My Trip To The Lincoln Memorial.

reviews.title: Go in the evening - awesome experience
reviews.text: I visited the Lincoln Memorial in July 2025.  I have been to the Lincoln Memorial many times but never in the evening.  I took Uber to time my arrival ten minutes before sunset.  I walked along the Reflecting Pool to the World War 2 Memorial (not a good photo op because the fountains were off).  Then I walked back to the Lincoln Memorial which was already illuminated and took a photo.  I then went to the Korean War Memorial, the MLK Memorial and viewed the Jefferson Memorial and Tidal Basin from there.  All illuminated and many photo ops.  Then I walked back to the Lincoln Memorial.  By then it was darker and the illumination was even more dramatic.  I walked up the steps to view Lincoln and it was very well lit.  I got an awesome photo of the Washington Monument with the Reflecting Pool.  By then it was after 10 pm and I got an Uber back to my hotel.  Visiting the Lincoln Memorial and the other memorials and monuments during the evening is an awesome experience.

reviews.title: To Abraham Lincoln, saviour of the country!

This Greek temple with its whiteness and columns houses the remarkable statue of President Abraham Lincoln (1809-1865), by Daniel Chester French. This memorial was inaugurated on May 30, 1922.The famous president is sitting there, with this serious attitude and his piercing look made of his sunken eyes. This man of good stature seems to be finally enjoying a moment of peace and seeing with hope the rest of things for his country.

reviews.title: A Powerful Tribute to American History 🇺🇸

Standing before Lincoln’s statue and reading the inscriptions from his famous speeches reminded me of the enduring values of equality and freedom.The site is very accessible and well-maintained, with plenty of space to sit, reflect, and take in the significance of it all. I highly recommend taking a moment to simply stand still and absorb the meaning behind this national treasure.Tip: Go early in the morning or later in the evening to avoid crowds and enjoy the best lighting for photos!

reviews.title: Impressive Memorial to Our Greatest President
reviews.text: If you have to choose one monument to visit in Washington DC, it should be the Lincoln Memorial. A fitting tribute to arguably the greatest president in the history of the country. Completed in 1922, it is a beautiful marble structure with the appearance of a Greek temple. In addition to the massive sculpture of Abe, engraved on the inside walls of the memorial are two of his most famous speeches, his Second Inaugural Speech and The Gettysburg Address. The view from the steps of the memorial of the Reflecting Pool and National Mall with the Washington Monument and Capitol Building in the distance is incredible. This has also been the sight of many protests and historic moments in the civil rights movement including where Martin Luther King delivered his "I Have a Dream" Speech in 1963. The Lincoln Memorial takes on an extra level of beauty after dark when it is illuminated. It is also less busy than during the day. It is pretty cool to walk around the backside of the memorial so that you can see the Eternal Flame at Arlington Cemetary burning in the distance across the Potomoc. The Memorial can be visited 24 hours a day although Park Rangers are available from 930am-10pm. The nearest Metro is at Foggy Bottom which is a 17-minute walk away.

reviews.title: The Lincoln Memorial: A Must See Attraction
reviews.text: One of the most visited and most photographed attractions in Washington DC is the Lincoln Memorial. The large stone structure and the statue of Lincoln, seated in a chair, are images that most everyone will recognize. Approaching the Lincoln Memorial, you will need to be prepared to walk some steps. It seems like a lot from a distance, but once you get closer and start walking up the steps, it’s not bad at all. If you cannot walk the steps, due to being in a wheelchair or any other reason, this is not a problem because there is also a ramp. Once inside, you will be presented with the large statue of Lincoln, which takes center stage. Surrounding the statue are important quotes, including Lincoln’s famous Gettysburg address. Some will spend time reading this and other quotes, but the majority of people who visit will simply pay their respects to one of our greatest presidents, snap a few pictures, and continue on to other attractions.The Lincoln Memorial is an iconic attraction, to be certain, and it is offered free of charge. The large pillars on both the outside and inside of the building make you feel like you are entering a shrine, a holy place. Everyone is familiar with the Lincoln Memorial and most already know what it looks like from all the shared photos, but it is still a must- visit place for your next visit to Washington DC.

You can walk up the stairs or the ramp to get to the top. They were in the process of rebuilding the museum in the undercroft of the monument. Due to this, the stairs had coverings for the construction. After heading up the stairs, you see the fairly large seated Lincoln inside the building. There wasn't much else in the building other than the statue. The walls on both sides did have inscriptions. The view after heading out is quite nice, with the Washington Monument in the distance and the poll just in front.It is worth a stop since it is something that is seen quite a lot on TV and does look nicer in real life.

reviews.title: Best Tribute to A Great American Leader
reviews.text: Lincoln Memorial is located in the west of National Mall in Washington DC. The statue is in the memory of America's 16th President and one of the greatest leaders of the country who began the struggle for racial equality and justice for the black people of America. The 99 feet high marble statue of Lincoln sitting on a chair and high pedestal is housed inside a large hall that is surrounded by 36 Doric style columns representing the number of states at the time of his death. He survived the Civil War between the northern and southern parts of the America and sacrificed his life for the enslaved and downtrodden people of America, justifying the epitaph inscribed on the wall behind his statue that reads- 'In this temple in the hearts of the people for whom he saved the Union the memory of Abraham Lincoln is enshrined forever.' There are large murals with inscriptions on the other two side walls representing Gettysburg speech and Inaugural Address. In one of the steps outside the statue is inscribed, " I have  A Dream" the famous words of Martin Luther King Jr.

reviews.title: Visit Washington, DC - it’s amazing
reviews.text: Visiting Washington, DC, with my wife and our two young kids (ages 6 and 7) was an incredible experience! The historical monuments like the Lincoln Memorial, Jefferson Memorial, and Washington Monument were breathtaking. It’s something else to see these landmarks in person, especially with little ones—they were awestruck. The National Museum of Natural History was a huge hit with the kids; the exhibits are engaging and really brought the wonder of history and nature to life for them.The Air and Space Museum was partially under construction, so it didn’t have quite the “wow” factor we were hoping for. However, spending a few hours in Alexandria turned out to be a pleasant surprise; the quaint streets and charm gave us a bit of variety and made the trip even more memorable.Two downsides were parking and the cost of eating out. Parking can be a hassle in DC, so I’d recommend planning for that ahead. Dining out is on the pricier side, so families might want to budget accordingly or consider some packed meals. My biggest piece of advice? Dress comfortably and wear good running shoes—there’s a lot of walking, and you’ll want to be ready for it.Overall, this was one of our best family vacations yet! The blend of history, culture, and adventure made it unforgettable.

reviews.title: True Hero
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is an iconic tribute to one of America’s most revered presidents. The majestic monument, with its grand steps and striking statue of Abraham Lincoln, offers a powerful and inspirational experience. The views of the Reflecting Pool and the Washington Monument add to the memorial's significance. It's a must-see landmark for anyone visiting Washington, D.C., and a profound reminder of Lincoln's legacy and the ideals he stood for.

reviews.title: Solemn place
reviews.text: Lincoln Memorial is located in the Mall area. As with many monuments in the city, this one is designed in a classical style and closely resembles a Greek or Roman temple.  The 19-foot-tall statue of Lincoln looks out from a solemn chamber in a building surrounded by 36 columns, each representing a state in the union at the time of Lincoln's death. Admission is free and the Memorial is always open, except for Christmas. In addition to being a symbol of the city, it hosts many events and is famous for being the venue from where Martin Luther King Jr delivered the “I have a dream” speech in 1963. In this period the memorial is subject to important work for the construction of a museum dedicated to Lincoln. Despite the work the charm of the monument does not fail, it should be a bit more respectful and less noisy, remembering that it is still a memorial. If there was more silence the place, with its beautiful view of the Mall, would be phenomenal.

reviews.title: Worth seeing and worth a visit!
reviews.text: Worth seeing and worth a visit. There was no waiting time and the visit is free. The height of the memorial and the design are impressive. Also, you have a very nice view of the Capitol. It's worth a visit.

reviews.title: Trip with two teenage boys in DC
reviews.text: My husband & I took our grandsons, 12 & 14 to DC so they could enjoy and experience our nation's capital. We had 3 full days and we really filled them. We stayed in the Capital Hill/Navy Yard area which does have many restaurants, is close to a Metro station as well as the Baeball stadium. For the Air & Space museum get tickets ahead - it gets full so ticket/passes are needed (free). we go to the Hirschorn Modern Art museum, The Potrait Museum, The Holocaust Museum, American History museum. Also had a tour of the White House as well as the Capital. The Capital tour was a big hit. Made it to most of the monuments during the day but also went back at night because they are stunning at night. Last museum was the International Spy Museum (not a mithsonian and $ticket needed. Went to the National Zoo too, although if short on time skip it. Eastern Market (Capital Hill) is a great stop too. We never made it to Georgetown - next time! (I've been there many times so I didn't mind)  Our boys were very engaged at all the Museums - thrye loved Spy Museum.

reviews.title: Guess it’s a must see

While I deeply respect and appreciate this presidents efforts and achievements, I shy away from the efforts to turn this memorial into a place of worship. Fitting, though, it is built on stilts to make it appear elevated in the landscape. And even more interesting, they are now working on turning the vault under the structure into an exhibition area, including the graffiti left from the workers who built it.

reviews.title: Another Bucket List Site
reviews.text: I had eagerly looked forward to to the Lincoln Memorial, Pres. Lincoln being my most revered President. We were there around sunset, so the picture-taking wasn’t the best. There was a huge accessible ramp constructed to bypass construction taking place, and construction fencing and barriers blocked part of the view of the iconic memorial and statue from below. I walked up the stairs to the inside, though the lighting inside wasn’t great for my pictures at that time of day. I was somewhat dismayed at the numerous teenage students who were milling about, shouting and laughing, and taking selfies, showing no reverence or thought for where they were. Still, standing at the foot of the statue was an awe-inspiring experience to see & ponder. I’ve very glad I went there, and would recommend as a Must-See memorial in Washington DC.

reviews.title: A Must See in Washington DC
reviews.text: We visited twice, once on our own in the day time and later, on a night time tour.  Both times it was crowded (though less so at night).  In the day time it was very crowded, and it is worth patiently navigating your way through the crowds to view this impressive monument up close and take in the speech inscribed in stone, and other information about the 16th President.  (A little useful tip: underneath, there are public toilets - not always easy to find in US cities).

reviews.title: Park Police are strict!
reviews.text: I have lived in Washington for 20 years, and used to work in very close proximity to this Monument for almost 15 of those. So I have been to this Monument many times, and sat on its steps to eat lunch and have gone during work hours just as a little break to sit back and awe at. Of course I have taken several guests there at night, and it's really beautiful and a magical place to be. I do recall hanging out at the monument with an ex-boyfriend and we had coffee with us. We attempted to sneak around to the back side and consume our hot beverages during the cold weather as it was raining. It really would have been a truly romantic evening and a much more memorable experience had the Park police not kicked us out for having food and drink, or rather drink on the premises. This was just coffee mind you and nothing illegal. We weren't doing anything else other than just wanting to have a private defensive place to sit and enjoy a record and the Magical atmosphere. So if you do go, I recommend you don't bring any hot beverages, or any food or beverage that would be consumed on the monument premises. It's a wonderful place to go and be pensive, but I think they want people to just come up see Mr Lincoln, take a few pictures and then go.

reviews.title: Wonderful memorial!

The architecture of the building itself is gorgeous and that is only enhanced by the statue of Lincoln himself. My favorite way of seeing this is it lit up at night and the memory of that is one that I will keep with me forever. It's a beautiful memorial and one you should make sure to see once in your life.

From the Lincoln Memorial you can have a wonderful view on the Washington Memorial and the reflecting pools.I would recommend visiting it in the evening, too. It looks really spectacular. All memorials in Washington are free of costs.

It's crowded with schools and other visitors day and night, and it's genuinely time-consuming to get there and back via walking (unless you're looking for a lengthy walk, which you might be). But it's worth it for sure. Say what you want about glorifying the founding fathers of any country, but you FEEL the glory standing in front of this statue. You have to wonder if Honest Abe would like this monument, and I imagine he wouldn't really be a big fan of it personally. But his accomplishments certainly warrant his commemoration, and this is a more-than-worthy way to do so. reviews.title: A wonderful and fitting memorial honoring Abraham Lincoln
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C. is located at the western end of the National Mall at the opposite end of a long grass strip from the Capitol building. Visiting the Lincoln Memorial can be challenging if you are driving since finding parking can be a challenge due to its central location. I recommended utilizing public transportation or parking at nearby garages and lots, such as the Union Station Parking Garage or the Ronald Reagan Building and International Trade Center Parking Garage. You could also take a guided tour or utilize ride-sharing services. I rented a car and toured several sites that eveningThe main entrance to the monument is by broad steps on the eastern entrance. As you approach the memorial, the grandeur of the structure becomes increasingly apparent. The iconic 19-foot seated statue of President Lincoln commands the attention of all who visit. The larger-than-life figure exudes a sense of strength and wisdom, while the inscription of his immortal Gettysburg Address and Second Inaugural Address reminds us of his profound impact on the nation.The memorial's interior is a large chamber, adorned with murals depicting significant moments from Lincoln's life. The marble walls and wide spaces create an atmosphere of reverence and reflection. From the steps of the memorial, visitors are treated to panoramic views of the Reflecting Pool, the Washington Monument, and the U.S. Capitol, forming a breathtaking vista that encapsulates the spirit of the nation. It is not only a tribute to a remarkable leader but also serves as a gathering place for historic events and peaceful demonstrations. Its significance in American history and its architectural grandeur make it a must-visit destination for locals and tourists alike. The lighting on the steps at night is very limited so step carefully. If you were only going to see one monument in DC, I would choose this one.

reviews.title: Crowded but must-see
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is a monument in Washington DC dedicated to Abraham Lincoln, the 16th President of the United States. It is located on the National Mall and is one of the most popular tourist destinations in the city.When there are a lot of people at the Lincoln Memorial, it can be a bit crowded and hectic. Visitors may have to navigate through crowds and lines to get inside the monument, especially during peak tourist season.Despite the crowds, the Lincoln Memorial is still a must-see destination. The monument is an impressive structure with 36 white marble columns and a large statue of Abraham Lincoln inside. The walls are inscribed with some of Lincoln's most famous speeches, including the Gettysburg Address and his Second Inaugural Address.Visitors may need to be patient and wait their turn to get a good view of the monument or to take a photo. However, the crowds also add to the energy and excitement of the experience.One tip for dealing with the crowds is to visit the monument early in the morning or later in the evening, when there are fewer people around. This can also provide a more peaceful and serene experience, and allow visitors to take in the beauty and grandeur of the monument without the distractions of large crowds.Overall, the Lincoln Memorial is a must-see destination for anyone visiting Washington DC, and despite the crowds, it's worth the effort to visit and pay tribute to one of the most important figures in American history.

reviews.title: Washington's most beloved monument?

reviews.title: A Must-See on the Washington Mall
reviews.text: We visited in Fall season, and if you have the chance I'd suggest you do the same, as this can  be a very busy area of the Washington Mall. If you visit the Washington DC Metro website, you'll be able to see that the train and bus lines make stop/s along the Mall.  I remember the 1st time we were in DC about 10 years ago, We bought what was I think a multi-day pass, used the heck out of it, and our car didn't leave our hotel the whole time we were there!But, back the the Lincoln Memorial.  It wasn't as crowded, as I stated the BUSY tourist season was over.  Such a beautiful building.   If you're able, take the time to walk around like we did, and take in the different views of the city at every turn.  Also, don't forget a good pair of shoes and have you phone charged, as you'll be taking SO many photos.

reviews.title: Missed out
reviews.text: Went to DC recently to see a bit of history. Well a bit is all we saw. Travel through DC is a challenge to say the least. No one there seems to be tolerant of any type of traffic, so if you slow down to be sure you're turning on the right street because you're from out of town, or you slow up just to look at a site, you are honked at, yelled at, and given the finger. Lovely welcome for tourists - thanks!So after two days of fighting traffic and rude people, we cut our vacation two days short and decided if we were going to get to see any of the monuments or sites, we'd have to leave the hotel to get on the road before daybreak so no one would get mad because we were holding up traffic.We left our hotel at 4:00 A. Knowing nothing would be open to tour, we still wanted to get pictures of the more popular sites, such as the Lincoln Memorial. Imagine our disappointment when we found out you can get pictures of every side of the monument from the road/car EXCEPT the side old Abe is actually sitting on. Unfortunately, I am not able to walk a great distance, so even in the regular business hours, I wouldn't have been able to walk up any steps, but I had hoped to at least view the memorial from the car and get pictures. Nope, not able to do so. Not that we could see, anyway, but it's hard to see everything in the dark.Not to mention, with all the security around DC in general (which obviously is a good thing) you don't really push to try to get in somewhere that looks inaccessible as you don't know for sure if it looks that way by accident or on purpose, because you won't want to end up in custody for fear of them thinking your there to do some dastardly deed.The sheer size of the building is amazing and breathtaking, but I sure do wish we had gotten to see Lincoln.

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial-Free Entry, Stunning at Night.
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is one of the top destinations in DC. Entry is free, and we decided to visit at night when the air was cooler and there was a bit of a breeze.The statue of Abraham Lincoln is much larger than it seems in photos, and the side walls are engraved with two of Lincoln’s speeches.  It is a place filled with honor and thoughtful reflection. Also, make a point to stop near the top steps to find the marked location where Martin Luther King Jr. delivered the historic “I Have A Dream Speech”.

reviews.title: One of my favorite monuments in DC

reviews.title: Iconic and perfectly placed
reviews.text: We walked here on our first full day in the city.  It's sited at one end of the mall, which is the focal point fo the city, and opposite the Capitol Building situated at the far end.  The memorial is breathtaking with Lincoln sitting prominent and powerful in the centre, looking out towards the Washington memorial in the centre.  You have to climb some steps to get up to the monument and, with Lincoln facing you, there is an engraving in stone on the wall on the right with his second presidential address and his Gettysburg address on the wall on the right.  There are lots of people selling water and Ice Creams outside.  There are restrooms at the base of the monument on the left as you look upwards.  However, due to the significant amount of use they get, they appear not very well maintained.  As a monument it is fitting to a man of great standing and an absolute must for anyone visiting the Mall.   We also visited at night when we did an evening bus tour. reviews.title: One of the absolute greatest monument buildings in the entire (history of the) world
reviews.text: PROS* Stand in awe at one of the world's most iconic famous and meaningful structures* Fantastic structure- an architectural marvel* Tremendous statue in thoughtful pensive pose- gigantic* A monument to our guiding principles and future as a nation* It feels like a temple or a shrine* A historical place to remember the events here through the ages* Unparalleled and unequaled views in both directions- the National Mall and towards Arlington National Cemetery* Learn about Lincoln from his speeches engraved on the walls and from the information downstairs* Free and unfettered access 24 hours a day* Celebrate its 100th anniversary in 2022* Bond with our nation's past and commit for a better future* Best later at night or early at dawn in the morningCONS* It can be always crowded* Tour groups (especially school groups) can be rowdy and disrespectful* Tour group guides speeches disturb the solitude that is an essential part of this shrine* Motorized and pedal bicycles roam freely at the base- dangerous* Truly inadequate lighting at night- dark! (see my many photos)- a danger for the visually- challenged"I VISITED THIS PLACE"...... as the first and most important stop on my nightime monuments tour for my family (we visited the adjacent Vietnam. Korea and MLK but did not get any further that night).  As stated and as seen in my many photos, the place after 2030/2100 was very crowded with noisy groups and it is quick dark and could be downright dangerous to thos who are disabled- and that was at night!!  Maybe everyone is learning of the secret to come at night, as I've posted on the TripAdvisor D.C. forum for years.So we returned at 0700 the next day and there were still plenty of people there, but it was much more managable, yet certainly not quiet nor solemn.  We walked around the entire perimeter of the building, at the level of the statue.This place deserves more than five starsTIPI've always said and written to go at night; now I add go at dawn PLEASE see my many photos- from night and from day and then from various lookouts, perches and observation points and backgrounds. reviews.title: You can't appreciate its grandeur unless you've been there
reviews.text: How many motion pictures have you seen that featured the Lincoln Memorial? From Jimmy Stewart to Tom Cruise to Clint Eastwood? You simply can't appreciate the grandeur of the place unless you've been there. It is a very humbling experience. Located at the west end of the National Mall in Washington, D.C., it was built to honor Abraham Lincoln, the 16th president of the United States. Construction began in 1914 and completed in 1922. On of the city's major tourist attractions -- it drew 7.8 million visitors in 2019 -- it is open 24 hours a day and has been the site of many famous speeches, including Martin Luther King Jr.'s  "I have a dream" speech o August 28, 1963. The structure echoes a neoclassical Greek temple, features Yule marble quarried in Colorado and measures 189.7 by 118.5 feet and is 99 feet tall. It is surrounded by a peristyle of 36 fluted Doric columns, one for each of the 36 states in the union at the time of Lincoln's death in 1865, and two columns at the  entrance behind the colonnade. The columns stand 44 feet tall with a base diameter of 7.5 feet. Leading up to the shrine on the east side are the main steps, which begin at the edge of the Reflecting Pool. There are three chambers in the memorial's interior divided by two rows of Ionic columns each 50 feet tall and 5.5 feet across at the base. The central chamber, which houses the famous 19-foot-tall seated sculpture of Lincoln, is 60 feet wide, 74 feet deep and 60 feet high. On the walls are inscriptions of two well-known speeches by Lincoln, the Gettysburg Address and his second inaugural address. The memorial was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1966.

reviews.title: What An Iconic Memorial! Worth A Look!
reviews.text: The giant memorial to 'Honest Abe' is such an iconic structure that I had to visit when in Washington DC. It sits near The White House and on The Mall with The Washington Monument. Not to forget The Vietnam Veterans Memorial. An excellent picture of the The House of Representatives (The Capitol Dome) may be taken whilst at the memorial. All within walking distance. Some things I picked up on. It is in Greek Revivalist architecture (based upon The Parthenon in Greece), it has 36 columns because of the 36 states that were part of the union at the time of Abe's death, and has 58 steps, which represent his two years in office and being 56-years-old at the time of his assassination. Spend a morning or all day taking in these amazing structures. It really is great sight-seeing!

reviews.title: The Lincoln Memorial…

reviews.title: Very Meaningful Visit

There is a time limit.  I walked to the Lincoln Memorial.  I have been here many times.  I had just visited several Civil War battlefields so this visit had a lot of meaning.  The Lincoln Memorial was very crowded this time.  I read the words of Lincoln's Gettysburg Address and Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address.  The Lincoln Memorial book and gift shop was open.  The staff of the book and gift shop were very helpful and gave me National Park Service brochures.  Finally, I found the marker for Martin Luther King's "I Have A Dream" speech.  I had been searching for this in past visits and finally found it.  All in all a very meaningful visit to the Lincoln Memorial.

reviews.title: As Lincoln said For the People!
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is a US national memorial built to honor the 16th President of the United States, Abraham Lincoln. It is located on the western end of the National Mall in Washington, D.C., across from the Washington Monument. Taking the form of a neoclassical temple, the memorial's architect was Henry Bacon. The designer of the memorial interior's large central statue – Abraham Lincoln, 1920 – was Daniel Chester French; the Lincoln statue was carved by the Piccirilli Brothers.[3] The painter of the interior murals was Jules Guerin. Dedicated in May 1922, it is one of several memorials built to honor an American president. It has always been a major tourist attraction and since the 1930s has been a symbolic center focused on race relations. The history of this glorious building is more than incredible as the man who is depicted within it. Lincoln was a man of many attitudes feelings and ideals who was fought almost all the time. During the Civil War he had to actually fire a very famous General who was a friend of his. His name was McClellan, for some reason this general couldn't figure out when to fight!Lincoln it is said actually visited him and fired him replacing him with a big mouth cigar chewing General Named Grant! Well Grant got it done alright. We all know what happened to Grant now don't we?The building is in the form of a Greek Doric temple and contains a large seated sculpture of Abraham Lincoln and inscriptions of two well-known speeches by Lincoln, The Gettysburg Address and his second inaugural address. The memorial has been the site of many famous speeches, including Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech, delivered on August 28, 1963, during the rally at the end of the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom.Like other monuments on the National Mall – including the nearby Vietnam Veterans Memorial, Korean War Veterans Memorial, and National World War II Memorial – the memorial is administered by the National Park Service under its National Mall and Memorial Parks group. It has been listed on the National Register of Historic Places since October 15, 1966, and was ranked seventh on the American Institute of Architects 2007 list of America's Favorite Architecture. The memorial is open to the public 24 hours a day, and more than seven million people visit it annuallyThe day i was there I am an Opera singer. At the entrance of the memorial since it blocks out the sun, the statue is shrouded in the shadows so you can't really see it until you enter. Once you go inside, your eyes adjust to the dark, and then you see him, a huge statue but with a gentle face staring out at Washington. On the walls beside him are quotes from some of his famous speeches like the Gettysburg address and the sight has even more historical significance when you remember that MLK's I have a dream speech was held here decades ago. This memorial gives you a link to America's history, it's both majestic and educational.

reviews.text: My son and  visited the Lincoln Memorial on our recent trip to DC.  The Memorial is one of the signature monuments in DC.  It is a beautiful monument and grand in scale.  It sits at the opposite end of the National Mall from the US Capitol Building.  The memorial contains a very large statue of Abraham Lincoln seated in the center of the monument.  The statue is posed to reflect the two sides of Lincoln, the firm Lincoln who vowed to stop the Southern States from secession and the conciliatory and the kind Lincoln who wanted to welcome the Southern Stars back as brothers at the end of the Civil War. It is a very moving monument.  Also the views from the top of the steps are terrific.  You can see the reflecting pool and the Washington Monument and the Capitol Building and more.  This is a must see in Washington.
