reviews.text: This monument is immpressively large. Well guarded - guards with machine guns.Would have given it 5 stars but the condition of the woman's washroom on January 1st made me feel embarassed to be an American. Hopefully this was a fluke.

reviews.title: The Must See
reviews.text: The history behind Lincoln Memorial is inspiring, the father of the American union receives his recognition in an awe-inspiring moment in the heart of DC. The Lincoln sculpture is perfect and really realistic. When I was there it was raining and dark but no lights were on what was difficult for us to read the inscriptions on the wall. The Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. “I have a dream” speech monument, in the center of the stairs is really nice and represents the struggle of millions.

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial
reviews.text: An awesome historical sight! Easy to get too and worth it. The sight is awesome at night also, it's very lit up.

reviews.title: A must see
reviews.text: We tried to take our kids here last time we visited the area, but due to illness, we weren't able to see this monument. We are so glad we tried again and was able to see it this time. We loved this monument. The size is unreal and the work that went into making it is just amazing. We are glad that we stumbled upon the history of it near the bathrooms, otherwise we wouldn't have known about all the rich history. The size of the building overall is incredible. Although there were many people coming and going, we felt we were still able to stand and enjoy it and get good pictures.

reviews.title: Imposing — as you would expect
reviews.text: I would like to visit it again but very early in the morning before the tourist hordes arrive as it was way too busy when i was there and it detracted from the experience.

reviews.title: A well know monument to visit
reviews.text: The serenity of this memorial really hits you when are close to the heart of this temple, view that famous inscription, and marvel and the marble statue of the great man himself.  Do go and share the wonder - you will not be disappointed.

reviews.title: Favorite place to spend New Year's Day
reviews.text: I lived in DC for 7 years, and for 3 of those years I watched the sun rise on New Year's Day. It's a remarkably beautiful place, especially at sunrise in winter and sunset in summer. If you come here in. the morning after a fresh snowfall, it's magical. I try to avoid the place when there are lots of tourists.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: This is not to be missed. I didn’t know all the history behind this but we visited the small museum underneath and I learned a lot.

reviews.title: One of DC’s gem
reviews.text: It’s a good place for family or friends. You can walk around or just sit on the stairs and  and enjoy the reflecting pool view with the monument in the background. It’s a good experience on any given time of the day.

reviews.title: Amazing structure
reviews.text: Beautiful site a long walk from the capital building, but along the way there are many very important structures.

reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.text: The monument is so big. Always has a lot of people taking pictures. The view is amazing to the the reflection pool and Washington Memorial.

reviews.title: Great  Memorial
reviews.text: It was a stunning experience.Impressive, highly meaningful statute awakens the respect inside. We visited it by day and night, take time to walk around. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Favorite monument
reviews.text: Has always been and still is my favorite monument, so impressive! Love the area, which it has more than one restroom.

reviews.title: Stunning!
reviews.text: Worth the walk to visit this Memorial. The statue of Lincoln is impressive and humbling. Highly recommend going.

reviews.title: Great Memorial
reviews.text: A must go place when visiting Washington DC. The memorial in gorgeous and Lincoln statue impressive.

reviews.title: The incredible Lincoln
reviews.text: We visited this by day and in the evening. A historic spot not to be missed. Take time to read the manuscripts and reflect on what is said, the then, the now and everything in between.

reviews.title: Amazing site
reviews.text: Impressive site. Never went to visit last time and did today So glad we did. Cool place. Amazing history and the view ..is spectacular

reviews.title: Running Destination
reviews.text: Visible from the entire mall, this Memorial marks the Southern End. If one were to run around the Capitol and this Memorial, the loop would be about 5 miles. The running paths are safe, clean and well maintained. Except for the paths closest to the Reflecting Pool next to the Lincoln Memorial, which are covered in goose poop.

reviews.title: It's history, stupid!
reviews.text: What's to say? It's the Lincoln memorial. There is no substitute! If you need convincing, nothing I can say will fix that.

reviews.title: Beautiful to see but crowded
reviews.text: We went to Washington in December over Christmas break thinking it would be cooler and there would be less crowds.  It was cooler, in the 60's when we were there but that was warm for that time of year and people were out in droves because of it.  The reflecting pool makes for GREAT pictures.  I just wish there had been less people in the picture.  Everywhere in the Mall area is a hike so be prepared!  I suggest if you are older and don't excersize much, start walking a couple miles regularly before you go.  Even if you are taking a shuttle or other transportation, it is a hike from parking lots to monuments.  In the area of the Lincoln Memorial is the WW1, WW2 and Korean War Memorials and the Washington Monument is at the other end of the reflecting pool.  All very walkable even for us 50+ but you had better prepare.  Definatly worth the effort!

reviews.title: Beautiful and awe inspiring
reviews.text: We visited the Lincoln Memorial on a gorgeous afternoon in December. We walked from the portrait gallery to the memorial – it’s a lot farther than you would think. We passed the world war two memorial and also visited the Vietnam veterans wall. The Lincoln Memorial It’s just all inspiring once you get up the steps and into the memorial. The book shop on the upper level was nice. And it’s a must see monument if you’re in the area.

reviews.title: Inspiring
reviews.text: This for me was the highlight of our trip.  The monument of Lincoln is awe inspiring and his words are moving.The view from the steps back onto the Mall are breathtaking.You can also stand where Dr. King gave his speech.  Loved my visit here.

reviews.title: Still inspiring
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial never gets old with three or four visits a year. If you are able to avoid busy evenings it is better. Don’t expect for it to be as serene as it was in Mr. Smith goes to Washington, but it it’s still moving, especially if you take the time to read the walls.

reviews.title: Beautiful piece of history
reviews.text: We went to visit Lincoln Memorial in April. It was pretty warm that particular day but it was worth it. The walk of the National Mall was tiring but very educational for our kids that are 7 and 9 years old. A must visit place  for al ages.

reviews.title: Beautiful at night
reviews.text: Love this place. Beautiful at night when you can look over at the Washington Monument. Only problem is it is a long walk to get there

reviews.title: Beautiful at night!
reviews.text: We decided to go to the Lincoln Memorial at night with our teens. It did not disappoint! Breathtaking views! We felt safe visiting at night too!

reviews.title: Spectacular!
reviews.text: A beautiful landmark to visit! We went at night which had a dramatic feel. The view of the Washington monument was beautiful. Lincoln's memorial monument is amazing! Definitely get a guide to fill you in on the historical architectural facts. Very interesting!

reviews.title: Always Impressive.
reviews.text: We brought visiting teenagers downtown for the first time and they enjoyed the Lincoln Memorial. It was mid to late afternoon on a Saturday, so pretty crowded. I love the immensity of the place, and the reminder to not forget an important piece of our past.

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial at Night
reviews.text: Went to see the sites at night while they were lit up. Fantastic. So quiet and smaller crowds. Always wanted to see this monument, really enjoyed it.

reviews.title: Great
reviews.text: This memorial is really impressive . I love this place . It’s beautiful and peaceful . When you stand next to the Abraham Lincoln statue you feel powerful. Better to go early to avoid the crowd .

reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.text: Quite a meaningful experience. If you read up a bit on your history you get more out of it. We went at night and were quite surprised about the crowds everywhere. Yes it was holiday week but was a worthwhile trip.

reviews.title: Loved it
reviews.text: The place is still fantastic, inspiringly awesome. The views are wonderful.  Lots of people but all understanding and not pushy.

reviews.title: See at Night and Day
reviews.text: A MUST see at night and during the day. Total different experiences. Both equally amazing. Grab some hot coco and sit on the steps in the evening. Its really nice and beautiful.

reviews.title: Busy!
reviews.text: This is the most popular site so expect lots of people. We went towards the end of our day at around 7pm thinking it would be quiet! It wasn’t. If you want it to yourself, go at 6:00 a.m. to be fair everyone is very considerate and you can all get the picture you want for the album! Well worth it as it really is iconic.

reviews.title: So much history!
reviews.text: The Reflecting Pool & Lincoln Memorial were the last stops of my first day in Washington DC. Get a glimpse of the 19-foot statue portraying Lincoln and stand on the very steps, where Dr. Martin Luther King gave his famous speech ' I have a dream '.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Beautiful and well maintained. There is an elevator and restrooms to the left of the front of the building. We saw it at night and during the day.  The only downside was we were visiting Thanksgiving week and it was crowded.  Impossible to get a great picture with other people in your shot.

reviews.title: Monumental
reviews.text: A monument worth visiting during the day and in the evening. Impressive, monumental, nice lighting in the evening

reviews.title: Impressive.  Makes you think.
reviews.text: The walk towards the Memorial is impressive.  The reflection pond and the trees getting to it are quite lovely.  Lots of steps of course but should be done at least once.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: More than lived up to expectations. A wonderful tribute to an inspirational figure of American history. Cracking view back across the mall to the Monument and Capital Building beyond

reviews.title: Historic and beautiful
reviews.text: A must place while visiting the capital . Try and go in the day and after sunset to see the reflection pool.

reviews.title: Big Building with Massive Statue
reviews.text: We visited the Lincoln Memorial and I personally wanting.  I did not know what to expect, and so was somewhat disappointed when we arrived there.  There was a massive building in the form of a roman or greek structure.  The statue of Lincoln is massive as is the structure.  For those that don't know, he is sitting on a chair looking  out.  On either side of the structure, there is the Gettysburg address and other side has his 2nd inaugural speech.  If anyone wanted to bother reading either speech it was available.  More people interested in taking a photo in front of the statue.

reviews.title: Memorial of a popular President
reviews.text: Good to visit a beautiful memorial of a popular American president..popular place for all tourists visiting Washington..Long water body and surrounded by a well maintained park

reviews.title: Some history here
reviews.text: Great to come here and stand where Martin Luther King did and imagine 250,000 people crammed in. Also where Forrest Gump was! Nice to walk the length of the pool up to the ww2 memorial. Be prepared as it’s constantly busy.

reviews.title: An absolute must stop when visiting Washington DC
reviews.text: A great tribute to a great American President, wonderfully presented and displayed in an awesome location that is well worth the visit.  Somehow there is a real sense of history and American Pride hanging in the air, you can see that visitors are moved.

reviews.title: Gorgeous at Night!
reviews.text: We went at night to avoid crowds, but also because it’s one of the things available after the museums close at 5pm.  The walk along the reflecting pool at night from the Washington monuments and the WWII memorial is beautiful.  I felt completely safe as there were other people around.The best part is how beautifully illuminated the monument is.  It’s stunning in person and you have time to read and reflect without having to dodge people taking selfies.  And, as most of DC, it’s free!

reviews.title: Girgeous
reviews.text: Nice place with gorgeous view inside and outside the memorial, a must see if you are in DC. Plan on going on a sunny day for nice pics and to walk around the mall.

reviews.title: Great to visit again
reviews.text: This is actually one of the last stops I had on a whirlwind 2-days in DC. Hadn't visited the Lincoln Memorial in a two years. Heavy rain that day and chilly temps on this last visit Dec 21. Still, it takes your breath away to see Lincoln in grand scale every time. Small hidden gift store inside has a remarkably well stocked collection of books and souvenirs.  I agree with others- even in the cold, its nice to stand at the top and take in DC

reviews.title: Majestic
reviews.text: Breathtaking! A grand structure for lovers of history and architecture. It’s close to other notable memorials and tourist location as well, so it’s a great midpoint pit stop too!

reviews.title: Greatest view of DC
reviews.text: By far the best view of DC. Standing in the stairs looking across the reflection pond is incredible. Had it not been in December I could have sat there all day. I would recommend going towards sunset so you can see during the day and night.

reviews.title: Patriotic
reviews.text: I love this place! Amazing sculpture and relaxing just to hang out at the reflecting pool. Just hard to take pictures without the photo bombers

reviews.title: Tried and True
reviews.text: This is a great spot to visit during anytime of year. So much history to take in.  This was a great spot to people watch, and learn a few things you won't learn in school.

reviews.title: A must
reviews.text: I doubt if anyone gets to Washington without visiting this memorial. Lincoln is still sitting majestic overlooking the Mall.

reviews.title: American Icon
reviews.text: Everyone has seen this in pictures and on the back of our pennies. A tribute to a great American this monument is as iconic as the man.

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.text: Great visit to Lincoln Memorial. Try to visit in early hours otherwise from 11am on it is crowded. Forewarning you will be dodging people on scooters everywhere so be on the look out. There is also a tiny gift shop to the right once up the stairs and at the monument. Overall great experience.

reviews.title: So majestic! Make sure you find the hidden detail on Lincoln's statue
reviews.text: If you stand on the wall side of the last column on the left, look at the back of Lincoln's head. Many say you can see Robert E. Lee's profile looking towards Arlington mansion! I see it!

reviews.title: Leaves you speechless!
reviews.text: The enormity and magnitude of the Lincoln Memorial will leave you speechless.  It is a MUST-SEE  when visiting Washington DC.

reviews.title: Great trip and things to see. Superb! Plenty to see and do
reviews.text: Great trip!Outstanding It’s the capital of our great country!!!! Nothing else is necessary to say!!Saw numerous monuments

reviews.title: Impressive!!!
reviews.text: This was the first time I've visited at night and it did not disappoint!!!  The memorial is always populated and open and is well maintained!!!  The steps are easily maneuverable and there is plenty of space for all visitors.

reviews.title: Nightime viewing
reviews.text: What an amazing monument and to visit at night added more to the experience. A must for all ages to take a moment and stand before this magnificent tribute to a man who was ahead of his time.

reviews.title: Four score and seven years ago
reviews.text: Although the last time I was in DC was back in 1997. Lincoln still looks the same clean as a whistle. Although,  the elevator is as old as time, bathroom extremely dirty oh and the water fountains have never been replaced. One would like to believe that they would have replaced them. Maybe instead of the White House getting a fence replacement project. Disappointed that the grounds in several areas seem to be totally run down.

reviews.title: Run With Abraham Lincoln
reviews.text: Three way to go. 1. Park at Arlington Cemetery if you run early morning. Run straight across Memorial bridge to Lincoln and continue down our National Mall to Washington Monument (between is exactly 1 mile). Take in sights of Smithsonian, Museum of Natural History and you've gone another mile. 2. Park at phone parking above Reagan National on Potomac River. You can watch airplanes turn overhead to land. Sometimes you will see Marine 1 plus one. Run between GW Parkway and Potomac turn when you see Lincoln and head down the National Mall.3. Start at Oronoco Park in Alexandria and head toward power plant going along the Patomac. So nice that part. Then run around Reagan Airport and head across Memorial Bridge. You will see the golden guardian statues guarding access to Lincoln. Look for protector of the Union, US Grant.I always go around watching Lincoln who is watching us all.

reviews.title: Great view in a historic monument.
reviews.text: Lovely view.of D.C. area in a historic monument.  Need to get tickets in advance or in the morning because there is a limit on number of visitors that are let in each day.

reviews.title: An impressive structure
reviews.text: We visited in the evening when it was dark the building is beautifully lit, and it’s not difficult to access, there’s a ramp to the side and a lift from a small museum that gives information on the build over all and the historic moments that have happened at the structure. Quite a site to see in real life well worth the visit!

reviews.title: Americana at its best
reviews.text: What a great place to visit for the monument and to share an important part of Americana with many others.  Just a awesome experience.

reviews.title: Awe inspiring and majestic. A historical delight!
reviews.text: One of the must see historical buildings in DC. Just to be standing in front of the memorial, understanding the founding history of the US, and walking around this majestic memorial is enough to give you goosebumps!!The building is one of the must sees along the National Mall with the others being the White House, the Monument, The House of Senate, The Jefferson Memorial, The Smithsonian Museums, and (further back) the Martin Luther King Memorial. Highly recommend a visit if you’re in DC. Enjoy your trip!

reviews.title: One of the most moving memorials anywhere
reviews.text: Even if you've been there several times, the walk up the steps and then the view of Lincoln is still a very moving experience. An absolute must when you are at the Mall. Everyone still reads his words and though there are a lot of selfies, the Memorial still inspires some awe. The Vietnam Veterans Memorial -- the wall -- is just to the right as you face the Lincoln Memorial. Two very inspiring places.

reviews.title: Always amazing to see and such a site at night!
reviews.text: While we've seen it a number of times over the years. It's still amazing, with incredible architecture, and what a great huge carving of Lincoln.

reviews.title: Must see on your DC trip
reviews.text: The scale of the monument can only be appreciated in person, pictures and movies don't do it justice. Do your best to go early and avoid the crowds.

reviews.title: Always amazing to see
reviews.text: A visit with Lincoln is always amazing, the architecture is impressive and the sight of Lincoln is breath taking. I have visited several times over the years and he is one of my top 3 to visit. I do love the view of the Mall from the top of the steps looking back at the Capital.

reviews.title: A Spot to Honour History
reviews.text: We took the Circulator here, and then walked back towards the Washington Monument.  On a sunny Saturday it was too crowded, and lacked the reverence one might wish.  Lots of selfie takers.  Take time to take your shots, up, down and all around.  Consider the impact of Lincoln and how America might have been without him.  Read the words of Lincoln on the interior walls -- today some should take more time to respect these thoughts.  A powerful place.

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial
reviews.text: It was pretty cool taking pictures at the Memorial. Lots of walking, but lots of great photo opportunities. Don't miss the exhibits on both sides of the memorial.

reviews.title: Jaw dropping and stunning
reviews.text: As the pictures show it can get very busy but once you climb those steps, you have a beautiful view of the memorial mall. It is such an interesting piece of history (one of many in dc) that you must visit. Just take your time with the walking as things appear closer than they are

reviews.title: Historic sight
reviews.text: This memorial is a must see for anyone visiting Washington. It is beautiful,  historic,  and offers a beautiful view of the reflecting pools, Washington monument and Capitol building.  I would recommend two visits, one in the day, and the other at night. It offers two different perspectives.

reviews.title: History and grandeur
reviews.text: After a lovely Walk along the National Mall the Lincoln Memorial looms on the horizon. It's one of those moments when you realise how big something is in real life! There are a lot of steps to climb to reach the top but there is also a (very old but safe) lift if the steps are too much. Totally worth it! A great way to learn more about the history of the US.

reviews.title: A must do in DC
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is just off Constitution Ave, so start at the Washington Monument, head west towards the World War II Memorial.  Then walk past the reflecting pod to the Lincoln Memorial.  At the top of the steps you will see a magnificent likeness of Lincoln, wait your turn then get close for some pictures.  When finished head down the steps where they have artifacts and great bathrooms.  You can do all of this in just a few hours.  Don't worry about the crowds everyone is very courteous.

reviews.title: Historic remembrance
reviews.text: Such a great place. The view from here is spectacular and reading the Lincoln's speeches are inspiring.

reviews.title: The Best
reviews.text: Always wonderful to see anytime of year with a great view of the Mall, Washington Monument, reflecting pool, etc.

reviews.title: This place is attractive and awesome
reviews.text: Lincoln Monument is built to pay tribute to America's president Abraham Lincoln. It is a very beautiful place, clean and secure, and huge. You will definitely get beautiful photos here.

reviews.title: Amazing Monument
reviews.text: This monument is amazing. It is an impressive sculpture of Abraham Lincoln. I think everyone should visit this monument.

reviews.title: Honouring Lincoln
reviews.text: Great monument in combination with reflecting pool. I visited it in morning and it was great in this light changing mood and little tourist around

reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.text: Loved this marvel close to the white house. It has abraham lincoln sitting on a chair and staring at the lake.

reviews.title: A Must for Everyone
reviews.text: Despite the heat and the crowds, you can't visit DC without a stop to see the Lincoln Memorial sitting at the top of the Reflecting Pond with the Vietnam, Korean War and WWII memorials nearby.

reviews.title: First visit
reviews.text: This was the wow factor when I saw Lincoln. It was just like the pictures but just more impressive in person

reviews.title: Night tour is way to go
reviews.text: We went at night while it was lit. It was a stop on a tour bus, well worth the $$, especially in the cold temperatures. The National Mall at night is beautiful.

reviews.title: One of the highlights of our trip!
reviews.text: Just awe inspiring to say the least. From the bike ride next to the reflecting pool through fall colored trees (ok, not all year but...) to the steps and then finally the monument itself. A must see for anyone visiting DC.

reviews.title: DC visit
reviews.text: Great place to visit, the statue is huge and the building as well. A place to read on american history.

reviews.title: Nice site
reviews.text: Stopped here during our Old Historic Trolley Tours and walked around the memorial and park. Very photogenic.

reviews.title: Elegant, Majestic, American!
reviews.text: I live in Washington and never or ever tire of this incredible edifice.  It's presence isuplifting and calming.

reviews.title: The Lincoln Memorial Enough Said
reviews.text: If your visiting the capitol either for you first time or returning then this will not disappoint, its grandeur and splendor is amazing, worth seeing in the day light as well as night time as all lit up is a amazing

reviews.title: Lovely, especially at night
reviews.text: Amazing view of the Washington monument and next to Vietnam memorial.  Very moving.  My 11 year old went in and read the Gettysburg address on the wall.  Very relevant.

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial at Night
reviews.text: Went on a nighttime monument tour while on vacation in DC.  I would strongly recommend visiting all the memorials at night first and return in day if you want more time.  The Lincoln at night was amazing and the right way to round out the tour; you also visit the WW II memorial which is also great at night.

reviews.title: Spectacular views
reviews.text: Like all of central Washington this is beautiful to behold . We were very impressed. As a capital city it is so splendid.

reviews.title: On our way to FL
reviews.text: We took the evening to drive in and through DC.  Plan parking in advance and walk the grounds in and around the White House and mall area. It’s HUGE!  Quite impressed.   Officers everywhere are very helpful with directions and or parking.

reviews.title: Very moving
reviews.text: Well worth a visit. There is an elevator for visitors with mobility issues. Very moving to see the speeches and inscriptions on the wall behind the statue.

reviews.title: Stunning masterpiece
reviews.text: We loved the writings inside to remind us of how far we've come and how far we have yet to go. Stunning views of the reflecting pool and monument.

reviews.title: Great Memorial
reviews.text: I was there late in the afternoon, so I was able to see the memorial in the day and night.  I really feel it’s more impressive at night.  It really glows and draws you in.  Sitting on the steps and looking towards the Washington monument is a very peaceful feeling.  Thankful for all the freedoms we have and thinking about all those who have been right there on those same stairs.

reviews.title: What a sight
reviews.text: Be sure you stop at the first landing heading home the main stairs. In the center is an inscription and it is where MLK Jr stood to give his I had a dream speech.

reviews.title: Grandiose monument
reviews.text: Seeing the statue up close is impressive and amazing! I never thought I will be so happy to see this historical monument so close!

reviews.title: Beautiful monument
reviews.text: This is a beautiful stop anyway, but to see it at night is amazing!  We did the trolley hop on during the day & their tour for the night time one too. They were also great to work with to get to the monuments.

reviews.title: Visit at dusk
reviews.text: My husband and I went at dusk, it was absolutely awesome! We look forward to bringing our children. The grounds are beautiful and the walk from the Washington memorial is great

reviews.title: A Monument Befitting Lincoln
reviews.text: A huge stone carving of Lincoln is housed in a Greek style temple in memory of his accomplishments in uniting the nation after the Civil War. There are restrooms to the left of the bottom steps. Just be aware, adjacent to the restrooms are more displays of Lincoln’s writings. We visited on a weekday morning where the crowd was surprisingly sparse and plenty of photo ops abound.

reviews.title: Great view
reviews.text: The building and the statue is big and very impressive. But too crowded if you want to wait for a good photo spot

reviews.title: Learn about us history
reviews.text: This the place you can learn about the history of United States. Like most of museums and monuments in Washington DC the Lincoln memorial is also a place you can visit without pay.

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text: Awe inspiring and breathtaking. Must visit in DC. Do visit both in day and night and take time to read the speeches engraved on either side of the walls.

reviews.title: He's Massive!!!
reviews.text: This is hands down my favorite monument!!! I've always loved Lincoln so that may have something to do with it!! Super cool to stand on the exact spot where MLK Jrs "I Have a Dream" speech!

reviews.title: Impressive site, small Lincoln
reviews.text: The whole parade up to the actual memorial is very impressive. The column building around the statue is also impressive. But once you are inside, it is amazing how small Abraham Lincoln is as a monument. He's suspended high because he is on a pedestal which is on a plinth, but the actual man himself is smaller than expected. This aside, the whole experience of walking up and going inside is amazing. Highly Recommend.

reviews.title: Wow!
reviews.text: It was even more glorious to see the Lincoln Memorial in person after many years of seeing it in books or on television.  It is overwhelming in its size and detail and leaves one awe struck.

reviews.title: Brilliant
reviews.text: The Memorial to the Capitol Building is a beautiful part of Washington from end to end. The walk between the two is long but absolutely worth it.The monument itself is as grand as you’d expect with some nice quotations (from the Gettysburg address and his inauguration?) on the walls.It’s pretty busy all the time but the views are stunning and great for photos.

reviews.title: WOW
reviews.text: This is a place I always saw on TV and wonderend about it in person.Being there was beyond any TV picture. You should go and see for your self

reviews.title: Must See
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is one of the most iconic and moving places I have ever visited. Lincoln's message still resonates today.  All of the amazing speeches and rallies that have been made there is very emotional.

reviews.title: Must see
reviews.text: Visited on Veteran’s Day.  Definitely makes one appreciate our country and the freedom we enjoy .  It was something that you will always remember

reviews.title: Must see
reviews.text: This was an absolute must see for us and we are so glad we did.  It was the highlight of our trip.  What a feeling and presence in this memorial.

reviews.title: Exceptional
reviews.text: Every US Citizen needs to see the Lincoln Memorial.  I actually felt his presence, and it brought tears to my eyes.

reviews.title: One of my favorite memorials!
reviews.text: I enjoyed my experience mostly at night because it allows you to reflect more on the Abraham Lincoln statue. If you come to DC, you cannot miss out.

reviews.title: One of the Greatest Monuments in America.
reviews.text: Just a Lifetime Experience to walk to this Monument behind the Pillars and See Abe Lincoln in Marble all lit up! Memory you will never forget, One of Americas greatest Experiences!

reviews.title: My Trip To The Lincoln Memorial.
reviews.text: This was another one of my favorite places to visit in Washington D.C. The atmosphere here is very clean, pretty, and scenic. Inside of the Memorial is The Seated Lincoln Statue and there are a few gift shops inside as well. The building is magnificient and you can't help but take a picture of it by the steps. On the other side of the monument is The Reflective pool and on the other side, you can see the WWII Memorial as well as both The Washington Monument and The Capitol Building (Capitol Hill).

reviews.title: Always a pleasure
reviews.text: I love being here a great deal. Especially watching the 4th of July fireworks. Sitting for 8 hours on the steps of the Lincoln, not even giving it a second thought with the pain in your legs, lol! I could stay at the memorial all evening. Watching the sunset, learning from all that is around me. Lincoln himself surrounded by his speeches.

reviews.title: Classic
reviews.text: A classic monument of D C. It’s usually very busy but you can get a great view at a distance too. Great place to start a tour of the mall.

reviews.title: Strolling on a winter afternoon
reviews.text: Spent a Saturday afternoon strolling.  Unfortunately, most of DC shuts down at 5 pm.  So ai didn't have time to do a museum.  Headed to Lincoln Memorial.  Tip: if steps are a  challenge, there is a tiny entrance on the left side to restrooms and an elevator.  I had to wait about 10 minutes but it beat climbing with a bad knee.  Another tip, when looking towards the Washington Monument, go to either the left or right corner of the Lincoln and look back. You'll see the Capitol dome beside the Washington ... Perfect for pictures.  Walk to the back side and you can see Robert E Lee's Arlington House across the Potomac at the Arlington cemetery.

reviews.title: Impressive inperson
reviews.text: We went to the Lincoln memorial twice, first at dusk and then during the day.  On both occasions it was very impressive.  The scale and quality is quite affecting, combined with the key extracts from speeches the memorial is a testament to one of America's great leaders. Make sure you don't miss the place where Martin Luther King delivered his I have a dream speech. It is commemorated with a tile on the floor near the entrance of the memorial. Most people.missed it whilst we were there. The view across the reflecting pool to the monument is also impressive from the top of the memorial steps.

reviews.title: Veterans Day Visit to DC
reviews.text: Amazing . Elevator to statue if you can't walk the stairs. Other memorials within walking distance. Great view of the relection pond and Washington Monuement.

reviews.title: Wonder what Lincoln is thinking about our nation today
reviews.text: What is listed in the topic area was exactly what my 12-year old daughter said after reading the great words of one of the most incredible leaders of our nation- a divided nation. If you are able to- take a tour with a park ranger many valuable nuggets of information.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: I loved walking up the stairs to the inner walls to read and take in the history The view from the top of the Stairs is amazing It is a must if in DC

reviews.title: Very interesting place
reviews.text: Never been in Washington DC and of course never at Lincoln M. But I liked that very much and I breathed the spirits of states founders and activists. Great panorama and sunny days. I liked it.

reviews.title: American history is there. A must go.
reviews.text: It seems to be always full of people, but it is a place with plenty of space for pictures. You should enjoy the difefrent angles and perspectives, and read the walls, for some historical information.It is interesting to visit the lower side area where you find also the toilets (before stepping up the memorial area where the statue of Lincoln stands).There are some nice historical information, and the elevator for disabled people.

reviews.title: Busy and beautiful
reviews.text: Even on a slow day, the memorial was quite busy. Look for the typo on the wall! Gorgeous all around!!

reviews.title: Beautiful at night.
reviews.text: I love the restrooms in the basement. They need a good cleaning, but thankful they are there.  The walk is not that bad and there are plenty of places to sit and rest. If you’re looking down the reflection pool-to your left will be the Vietnam Memorial and to your right will be the Korean memorial. Next up towards the Washington monument. Is the WW II memorial-my favorite of all of them! The view of the Lincoln Memorial from here is lovely.

reviews.title: Iconic Memorial
reviews.text: One of then most iconic memorials in DC. Since my last visit many years ago, they’ve added a small indoor exhibit (near the restrooms) that displays several quotes from Lincoln, and describes the construction process. An added feature that I really enjoyed. A great memorial for evening photos, and for views the whole length of the Mall.

reviews.title: Casting Shadows
reviews.text: Definitely a must for the obvious historical and picturesque reasons. Target fall when DC isn't as hot like during the summer.

reviews.title: Must See
reviews.text: Take time to read the inscriptions on the walls. The climb will get your blood moving. It is worth it though.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: Everyone needs to see this site.....beautiful landmark in our nation’s capital! The crowds did not affect our visit and those needing an elevator were comfortable going there.

reviews.title: It’s pretty nice!
reviews.text: I enjoy the memorial, but so many people were around that I barely saw it! It bothers me how messy it is!

reviews.title: It gives good vibes and motivation
reviews.text: This is a place charged with positive vibes, powerful spirit and very american! Loved it and it impressed the most my Romanian boy of 9 years old at his first visit in US

reviews.title: Unmissable
reviews.text: This was the first monument we visited after checking in to our hotel.  Two days later we took a tour and visited it at night. On both occasions it was awe inspiring.

reviews.title: Do not miss this Memorial to a great President
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is a beautiful, imposing open-air building containing one of the most iconic statues in the US. I have seen it in pictures and film all my life, but being there in person is an experience not to be missed.

reviews.title: Big
reviews.text: I hope that title sums it well, it's big. Of course it's not just big, when you're up close it's spectacular in its detail. We could not have imagined coming to DC without seeing it.

reviews.title: Like most monuments in DC, see it at night!
reviews.text: There are few things in Washington quite as iconic as Abe Lincoln. Definitely, go at night if you can. No matter how beautiful this monument is during the day, nothing can compare with its beauty at night. Stunning.

reviews.title: Wonderful
reviews.text: The National Mall is remarkable. All the memorials are worth visiting and it was interesting how close they look but it is a bit of a walk to see them all. Scooters are available all over the place.

reviews.title: Outstanding
reviews.text: This is definitely worth visiting.  The scale of the memorial is great and the significant speeches made by Lincoln are engraved on the walls.  Well worth reading and reflecting on in these interesting times.The view from the stairs over the reflecting pool is simply amazing.  The scale of the space is definitely impactful.  We had walked along the pool to get to the memorial and it was really nice to see.  There is a cafe nearby, which provided a bit of respite after all the walking and looking.  Nearby public toilets were not open, so don’t rely on these as part of your planning if you are going to spend time here

reviews.title: WOW
reviews.text: During our visit to DC, was saw the Memorial during the day, we returned at night the power of this memorial at night can not be put into words.

reviews.title: Must see
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial and the Washington Monument are a great place to make sure you stop by during your trip to Washington DC

reviews.title: Beautiful memorial
reviews.text: Very impressive memorial with a huge statue of Lincoln inside and a beautiful view of the Washington Monument. A must do in DC!

reviews.title: Family
reviews.text: What a fantastic building, the view from Washington Monument is fantastic and the walk down to the Lincoln monument is very interesting

reviews.title: The most magical monument ... at night!
reviews.text: The power of the Lincoln Memorial is best experienced at night! A place to reflect and get inspired by the achievements of President's Lincoln in abolishing slavery and the landmark speech of Martin Luther King. In these days of tough divisions amongst the US citizens, this is a place to visit, reflect and determine how we can each contribute our little bit to make the country better, united, and respectful... No better place either to contemplate the beauty of the Mall, all the way to the Capitol Building, especially at night and by moonlight!

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is a must see in Washington DC.  If you visit in the morning the sun will be more friendly to your photography.  Wear good shoes and go for it!

reviews.title: This is a must see!
reviews.text: We visited the Lincoln Memorial just after dark and it was quite a sight. The memorial is so big and the statue of President Lincoln is amazing with great details. What a wonderful tribute. Also, you can see the National Monument lit up and reflecting off the water. It was a great experience.

reviews.title: Must-see
reviews.text: Great views out onto the Washington Monument, with an awe-inspiring building right in the heart of the city. Powerful images and history respresented and made here. Crucial to visit.

reviews.title: Andy
reviews.text: Fantastic monument, and a must see at night. Stay for the 'park rangers' talk which is free and well worth waiting for.

reviews.title: Washington DC trip must!Washington DC trip must!
reviews.text: No trip to Washington can be complete without the Lincoln Memorial. Standing in front of Lincoln and reading his words are always a humbling experience! Make sure and take a leisurely walk around the reflecting pool.
